A slower reading can keep their relationships clear without supplying an unverified pronunciation rule or pretending that all the consulted explanations agree.

words.workingGloss: deathless deeds, in the selected reading
joined with all, provisionally; unwavering union is another reading
unfailing provision in the selected reading; enduring enjoyment is an alternative

study.interpretationCare: The heading is kept separate from the four lines. Source differences include ਅਖੱਲ/ਅਖਿਲ, additional consonant marks and heading spacing; these still need qualified review. The reading of ਅੰਬ੍ਰਿਤ is independently supported and must not be silently changed to ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿੱਤ. Deathlessness here guarantees neither physical immortality nor protection from illness.
study.reflection: Which of the four descriptions becomes clearer when you pause between the similar-sounding words instead of treating them as repetitions?
study.teachBack: Name the new metre, distinguish ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿੱਤ from ਅੰਬ੍ਰਿਤ in this reading, explain the selected meanings of ਜੋਗੇ and ਭੋਗੇ, and identify the unresolved ਅਖੱਲ/ਅਖਿਲ difference.

simple.en: Unshakable sovereignty is followed by steadfast creative power, universal dharam and deeds beyond complete understanding. The first three descriptions give the address a sense of steadiness and breadth; the last keeps human understanding from claiming to contain it. The lesson concerns Divine qualities, not permanent authority for a person or institution.
simple.pa: ਅਡੋਲ ਰਾਜ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਅਟੱਲ ਸਿਰਜਣ-ਸ਼ਕਤੀ, ਸਰਬ-ਵਿਆਪਕ ਧਰਮ ਅਤੇ ਪੂਰੀ ਸਮਝ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਕਰਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਹੈ। ਪਹਿਲੇ ਤਿੰਨ ਵਰਣਨ ਅਡੋਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਆਪਕਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੇ ਹਨ; ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਸਮਝ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਵਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਗੁਣ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਹਨ; ਕਿਸੇ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਜਾਂ ਸੰਸਥਾ ਨੂੰ ਸਦਾ ਲਈ ਬੇਸਵਾਲ ਅਧਿਕਾਰ ਦੇਣ ਦਾ ਬਿਆਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Distinguish sovereignty, creation, dharam and the limits of human comprehension.
study.closeReading: The compact Charpat form continues, with ਰਾਜੇ and ਸਾਜੇ followed by ਧਰਮੰ and ਕਰਮੰ. The first pair relates enduring sovereignty to the act or power of creation. The second adds universal dharam and action that cannot be completely fathomed. They should not be reduced to four versions of the same idea. In particular, ਅਖੱਲ is selected through the attested all-or-whole sense, whereas ਅਲੱਖ concerns what cannot be fully perceived. The sound resemblance makes careful attention useful. The last line also qualifies the learner’s confidence: a short explanation can offer a path into the words without claiming to have exhausted what they praise.

words.workingGloss: universal dharam, in the selected reading
deeds beyond complete perception or understanding

study.interpretationCare: Another consulted text omits the doubled consonant marks in these four phrases; the source spellings remain unchanged. The universal-dharam reading and Neki’s unhindered-law emphasis are kept distinct. Divine sovereignty or mystery must not be used to shield human power from accountability.
study.reflection: Where can steadiness of commitment coexist with an honest admission that you do not fully understand?
study.teachBack: Explain the four descriptions separately and distinguish ਅਖੱਲ from ਅਲੱਖ. Describe why enduring creative power does not mean every created form is permanent.

simple.en: Giving, knowing, illumination and honour are brought together by the repeated word for all. The chhand moves attention away from a private claim on the Divine and toward an address that leaves no being outside its scope.
simple.pa: ਦਾਤ ਦੇਣਾ, ਜਾਣਨਾ, ਚਾਨਣ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਣ—ਇਹ ਚਾਰ ਗੱਲਾਂ ਸਰਬੰ ਦੀ ਦੁਹਰਾਈ ਨਾਲ ਇਕੱਠੀਆਂ ਹੁੰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਕੇਵਲ ਆਪਣੇ ਲਈ ਮੰਨਣ ਦੀ ਥਾਂ ਸਭ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਂਝੇ ਆਧਾਰ ਵਜੋਂ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Hear the four different actions within the repeated universal address.
study.closeReading: Every line begins with ਸਰਬੰ, but the word following it changes. Giving concerns what is received; knowing concerns what is understood; radiance concerns what becomes apparent; honour concerns worth and greatness. Reading only the repeated opening would miss these differences. Reading only the four endings would miss their shared reach. The short lines therefore offer a practice in keeping particular qualities and universal scope together. In the final line, the direction of honour can be read in more than one way: honour bestowed throughout creation, or honour directed toward the Divine. Keep the selected explanation visible without turning a poetic universal into a claim that everyone holds the same beliefs.

words.workingGloss: all; the inclusive reach repeated in every line
radiance or making manifest in this working reading
honour or greatness; the direction of honour has alternative readings

study.interpretationCare: These are original educational explanations, not an approved literal translation. Universal giving is not a guarantee of possessions; universal honour does not erase differences in human belief.
study.reflection: Consider someone whose work usually goes unnoticed. What would it mean to recognise their dignity without expecting anything in return?
study.teachBack: Name the four qualities after ਸਰਬੰ and explain the two directions in which the final honour image can be read.

simple.en: The repeated address includes life, shelter, experience and connected presence. Its movement is relational: the Divine is praised not only as a distant protector but also as present throughout the life that is being protected.
simple.pa: ਇੱਥੇ ਜੀਵਨ, ਆਸਰਾ, ਅਨੁਭਵ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਹੈ। ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਦੂਰੋਂ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਨਹੀਂ, ਸਗੋਂ ਉਸ ਜੀਵਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੀ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਆਧਾਰ ਵਜੋਂ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Follow the progression from life to protection to shared presence.
study.closeReading: ਪ੍ਰਾਣੰ and ਤ੍ਰਾਣੰ sound close, yet they perform different work: life is followed by its shelter. The next pair changes the relationship again, introducing experience or enjoyment and then connection. This structure keeps the four short statements from becoming interchangeable slogans. The final ਜੁਗਤਾ gathers them into an image of presence with all. In reflection, distinguish the poem’s address to the Divine from a promise about what must happen to a particular person. The words can sustain gratitude and care without denying vulnerability. The enjoyer reading of ਭੁਗਤਾ remains a working choice; a nourishment-related interpretation should stay available for qualified review rather than being silently dismissed.

words.workingGloss: enjoyer or experiencer in the selected reading

study.interpretationCare: Life-breath imagery is not a breathing prescription. Protection is devotional language, not immunity from harm. Human needs for safety, nourishment and care remain real.
study.reflection: What act of care could make the word protection concrete for someone who is vulnerable today?
study.teachBack: Explain why ਪ੍ਰਾਣੰ and ਤ੍ਰਾਣੰ are not the same word, then describe how ਜੁਗਤਾ changes the sense of the whole stanza.

simple.en: Radiance stands beside mystery, and the ending of life stands beside nurture. The chhand asks the reader to hold each pair together rather than reduce the Divine to only what is visible, pleasant or easily explained.
simple.pa: ਚਾਨਣ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਭੇਦ ਅਤੇ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੇ ਅੰਤ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਨੂੰ ਕੇਵਲ ਦਿਸਣ ਵਾਲੀ, ਸੁਖਦਾਈ ਜਾਂ ਸੌਖੀ ਵਿਆਖਿਆ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਣ ਦੀ ਥਾਂ ਇਹ ਜੋੜੇ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਸੁਣਨ ਲਈ ਕਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Notice the paired contrasts without cancelling either side.
study.closeReading: The first two lines place ਦੇਵੰ and ਭੇਵੰ in a close sound relationship. Light can disclose a presence without making its depth fully available to explanation. The last two lines use a similarly close sound relationship between ਕਾਲੇ and ਪਾਲੇ, placing an ending beside continued nourishment. These pairs invite careful reading rather than an easy resolution of every difficulty. A reader may find one half of a pair more comfortable than the other; the text nevertheless keeps both. The movement from mystery to time and nurture also sets up the longer descriptions that follow at Chhand 79. None of this makes grief unreal or turns human violence into a spiritual act.

words.workingGloss: time or death; an enduring-presence reading is also attested

study.interpretationCare: The selected meanings remain provisional. Do not use the stanza to explain away another person’s grief, to claim knowledge of why a death occurred, or to justify harm.
study.reflection: Which is harder for you to acknowledge: that something may be present but mysterious, or that life includes both nurture and loss?
study.teachBack: Describe the two pairs and explain why interpreting ਪਾਲੇ does not require deleting the force of ਕਾਲੇ.

simple.en: The Rooaal heading introduces longer lines that join several descriptions at once. Origin without a beginning, universal honour, nurture and dissolution, and presence without attachment are brought into a single sustained address.
simple.pa: ਰੂਆਲ ਛੰਦ ਦੀ ਸਿਰਲੇਖੀ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਈ ਗੁਣ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਸਭ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਢ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਆਪ ਮੁੱਢ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਰਹਿਣਾ, ਸਭ ਥਾਂ ਮਾਣ, ਪਾਲਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਤ, ਤੇ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਨਿਰਲੇਪ ਰਹਿਣਾ—ਇਹ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Read each long line in meaningful phrases without changing the stored verse boundaries.
study.closeReading: The separate heading marks a change in poetic form; it is not a fifth verse. Within the first long line, ਆਦਿ and ਅਨਾਦਿ make a deliberate distinction between being the origin and being originated. The second line combines honour, radiance, mystery and generosity. The third refuses to isolate sustaining life from the fact that finite life ends. The fourth then joins presence everywhere with non-attachment and richness. These tensions give the stanza its depth. Read slowly enough to notice each term, but do not split the frozen four-line source into invented numbered lines. The word ਤ੍ਰਿਮਾਨ remains open to more than one threefold explanation, so the main teaching does not present one as settled.

words.workingGloss: unattached or detached in this context
rich in rasa or living savour; spelling retained

study.interpretationCare: The metre label is structural metadata. The threefold honour reading and the sense of ਘਾਲਕ require qualified review. Dissolution is attributed to the Divine, not to a person seeking power.
study.reflection: How might non-attachment allow you to care more freely, rather than care less?
study.teachBack: Explain the distinction between ਆਦਿ and ਅਨਾਦਿ, identify all three actions in the third line, and say why the heading is not counted as a verse.

simple.en: The stanza first removes the boundaries by which people usually identify something, then speaks of loving presence everywhere. Being beyond a particular name or place does not mean being absent, and freedom from binding attachment does not mean lovelessness.
simple.pa: ਛੰਦ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਉਹ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਹਟਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਅਸੀਂ ਕਿਸੇ ਦੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਾਂ, ਫਿਰ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਪ੍ਰੇਮਮਈ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਮ ਜਾਂ ਥਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੋਣਾ ਗੈਰਹਾਜ਼ਰ ਹੋਣਾ ਨਹੀਂ; ਬੰਨ੍ਹਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਰਾਗ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੋਣਾ ਬੇਪ੍ਰੇਮ ਹੋਣਾ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Distinguish freedom from limiting identity from absence of loving presence.
study.closeReading: The opening list moves through name, location, lineage and visible description. The next line changes direction, affirming primal presence, generosity, birthlessness and completeness. The third returns to limits, including country, clothing and attachment. Finally the fourth opens outward into every direction with ਅਨੁਰਾਗ. The poem therefore does not simply strip away everything and leave an empty statement. It moves from what cannot confine the Divine toward how love is present throughout existence. The juxtaposition of ਰਾਗ and ਅਨੁਰਾਗ deserves particular attention: a rejection of binding attachment need not be a rejection of affection. This is a reading of the stanza’s movement, not an instruction to abandon family or erase cultural identity.

words.workingGloss: complete or without remainder in this working reading

study.interpretationCare: No fixed identity is being declared spiritually inferior. The text’s Divine description must not become pressure on a person to reject family, clothing, ethnicity or needed human connection.
study.reflection: Notice a label you use for someone. What might you understand better by remembering that the person is more than that label?
study.teachBack: Explain why the first line can deny a limiting name while the poem still uses names, and distinguish ਰਾਗ from ਅਨੁਰਾਗ in this setting.

simple.en: The first half refuses to confine the Divine to a name or home while extending honour everywhere. The second half places the One beside the many: varied appearances do not exhaust or divide the reality being praised.
simple.pa: ਪਹਿਲੀਆਂ ਦੋ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਨਾਮ ਜਾਂ ਟਿਕਾਣੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਣ ਤੋਂ ਇਨਕਾਰ ਕਰਦੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਦਾ ਮਾਣ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਮੰਨਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਅਖੀਰ ਦੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਇੱਕ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਨੂੰ ਨਾਲ ਰੱਖਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ: ਅਨੇਕ ਰੂਪ ਉਸ ਇੱਕ ਹਸਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਮੁਕਾ ਜਾਂ ਵੰਡ ਨਹੀਂ ਦਿੰਦੇ।

study.focus: Track the movement from no fixed dwelling to many appearances and the remaining One.
study.closeReading: The stanza begins by refusing the ordinary ways of locating a person: a particular name, desire or home. It then repeats honour across all places and times. The final pair provides a positive image rather than leaving only negation: ਏਕ ਮੂਰਤਿ and ਅਨੇਕ ਦਰਸਨ place oneness and multiplicity beside each other. The last line uses the language of play to describe the unfolding and gathering of forms. This need not mean that the One first stops being one and later becomes one again; the teaching can distinguish changing appearances from their enduring ground. Keep this as a reflective reading of the wording, not a final decision about every philosophical question the stanza raises.

words.workingGloss: play; here an image for the unfolding of creation

study.interpretationCare: The image of play neither makes suffering unreal nor licenses indifference. The explanation is not an endorsement of an individual’s claim to supernatural identity.
study.reflection: When you meet people whose lives differ from yours, what might it mean to recognise shared worth without pretending their differences do not matter?
study.teachBack: Explain how ਏਕ and ਅਨੇਕ work together, and why the final play image is not a reason to dismiss someone’s suffering.

simple.en: The stanza asks how the unlimited can be known through limited descriptions. Scriptures, visible marks and family origins cannot provide a complete boundary around the Divine; the final line turns outward toward presence and authority across the worlds.
simple.pa: ਛੰਦ ਪੁੱਛਦਾ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਨੂੰ ਸੀਮਤ ਪਛਾਣਾਂ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਜਾਣੀਏ। ਧਰਮ-ਗ੍ਰੰਥ, ਦਿਸਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਿਵਾਰਕ ਮੁੱਢ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਹੱਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣ ਸਕਦੇ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਸੱਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Separate a limit on complete knowledge from rejection of study or respect.
study.closeReading: The first line names powerful sources of knowledge and still says that the Divine mystery is not fully known. The second then asks what method of outward identification would work when form, colour, caste and lineage do not fix the One. The third deepens the contrast by removing parentage and the cycle of birth and death. The final line is not simply another denial: it describes movement or ordering throughout the directions and recognition in the three worlds. The difficult phrase ਚੱਕ੍ਰ ਬੱਕ੍ਰ must remain visible as a translation problem rather than disappear behind a confident smooth sentence. A thoughtful reading can acknowledge the limits of a description while continuing to learn from it.

words.workingGloss: scriptural books beyond the Vedas in this context
manner or description in this provisional reading
the three worlds in traditional cosmic language

study.interpretationCare: The exact syntax of ਚੱਕ੍ਰ ਬੱਕ੍ਰ remains provisional. Traditional world-language is not an empirical map. Limits of scriptural comprehension do not justify contempt for scriptures, communities or education.
study.reflection: Recall something important that you understand only partly. How can recognising that limit make your questions more careful?
study.teachBack: Identify the three kinds of limitation discussed before the last line, and explain why uncertainty about one phrase should be stated rather than concealed.

simple.en: The stanza widens praise to the entire imagined cosmos while returning to the distinction between the beginning of creation and the beginningless Divine. Its final line places making and dissolution within the same address.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਉਸਤਤ ਨੂੰ ਸਮੂਹ ਬ੍ਰਹਿਮੰਡ ਤੱਕ ਫੈਲਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਰਚਨਾ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਢ ਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਅਨਾਦਿ ਹੋਣ ਦਾ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਮੁੜ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਘੜਨ ਅਤੇ ਸਮੇਟਣ ਦੋਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਸੱਤਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੱਖਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Read the cosmic scale as a widening of praise without confusing poetry and measurement.
study.closeReading: The opening invokes fourteen worlds to enlarge the range of the address. The second line then names the source of that expanse as both primal and beginningless. The third accumulates descriptions of purity, completeness and limitlessness before the fourth joins self-existence with the shaping and dissolution of the universe. Notice the repeated establishing language in ਥਾਪਿਓ and ਥਾਪਿ, then the paired actions ਗੜਨ and ਭੰਜਨ. The passage is not merely a list of impressive titles; it continually links the vastness of creation with a source not enclosed by creation. The reflective task is to recognise that scale without pretending the verse supplies a laboratory model or a timetable of cosmic events.
study.interpretationCare: Traditional cosmological imagery is not presented as scientific evidence. Purity is attributed to the Divine, not used to label communities or bodies as impure.
study.reflection: What changes in your priorities when you place a small concern within a much larger view of life?
study.teachBack: Explain why the Divine can be called ਆਦਿ and ਅਨਾਦਿ together, and identify the two complementary actions in the last line.

simple.en: Being beyond time and outward identity does not make the Divine description morally empty. The stanza joins freedom from limitation with dharam, the humbling of pride, resistance to wickedness and the gift of liberation.
simple.pa: ਕਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਬਾਹਰੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੋਣ ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਨੈਤਿਕਤਾ ਤੋਂ ਖਾਲੀ ਹੋਣਾ ਨਹੀਂ। ਛੰਦ ਇਸ ਬੇਹੱਦੀ ਨੂੰ ਧਰਮ, ਹੰਕਾਰ ਦੇ ਟੁੱਟਣ, ਦੁਸ਼ਟਤਾ ਦੇ ਵਿਰੋਧ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਦੀ ਦਾਤ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Follow the turn from what cannot limit the Divine to the ethical force of the final line.
study.closeReading: The first three lines repeatedly deny enclosure by time, place, material form, visible appearance or social classification. Yet the second line already names a positive relationship to ਧਰਮ. The final line makes that relationship more concrete by bringing pride, wickedness and liberation into view. Pay attention to the way similar-looking vocabulary changes with its context: ਕਾਮ here is provisionally understood as work or function, not as the desire denied elsewhere. Likewise, ਅੰਗ ਰਾਗ can be read as a compound concerning adornment or analysed into separate terms. These choices belong in the notes, not in a silent alteration of the source. Ethical reflection can begin with pride in oneself rather than a licence to brand other people as enemies.

words.workingGloss: the humbling or breaking of pride
work or function in the selected contextual reading

study.interpretationCare: No person receives a mandate here to punish those they call wicked. The selected readings of ਅਦੇਸ, ਅਭੂਤ and ਅੰਗ ਰਾਗ remain subject to qualified review; the Divine attributes are not guarantees of human invulnerability.
study.reflection: Where might pride make it harder for you to admit harm, apologise or change course?
study.teachBack: Describe the stanza’s movement toward the final ethical line, and explain why ਕਾਮ should not be given the same meaning in every passage.

simple.en: Depth beyond complete praise is joined to freedom from birth and bodily limits. The stanza also repeats the demanding pair of dissolution and nurture. Its difficult vocabulary asks for humility from the interpreter as well as from the reader.
simple.pa: ਪੂਰੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਡੂੰਘਾਈ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਜਨਮ ਅਤੇ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੋਣਾ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸਮੇਟਣ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਲਣ ਦਾ ਔਖਾ ਜੋੜ ਵੀ ਮੁੜ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਮੁਸ਼ਕਲ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਪੜ੍ਹਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਅਤੇ ਵਿਆਖਿਆ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਦੋਵਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਮੰਗਦੇ ਹਨ।

study.focus: Let the limits of praise also limit overconfident interpretation.
study.closeReading: The stanza begins with its own restraint: the One being praised is deeper than the praise can contain. That restraint matters when reaching ਅਨਾਤਮ, a term that should not be assigned a familiar modern slogan without argument. The working explanation keeps its relation to the neighbouring denials of bodily limitation and its affirmations of oneness and boundlessness. The last line then prevents a purely abstract reading by returning to power, ending and nurture. These are not qualities owned by a human speaker. A careful learner can understand the main direction of the stanza while also identifying which particular words need a qualified reader’s attention. Uncertainty made explicit is more useful than a falsely definitive glossary.

words.workingGloss: not a limited personal self in this provisional interpretation

study.interpretationCare: The ਅਨਾਤਮ and ਲਾਇਕ explanations are provisional, not settled scholarly translations. Bodilessness does not devalue disability or embodied life; descriptions of ending life never authorise personal violence.
study.reflection: Where could saying “this is my working understanding” make a conversation more truthful and more open?
study.teachBack: Explain the opening limit on praise, name the difficult term in line three, and show how the last line holds ending and nurture together.

simple.en: This stanza returns to the limits of description after praising presence, ending and freedom from outward guise. Accumulating more words does not give the mind possession of the unlimited, though study can still deepen understanding and humility.
simple.pa: ਵਿਆਪਕਤਾ, ਅੰਤ ਅਤੇ ਭੇਸ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਛੰਦ ਵਰਣਨ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦਾ ਹੈ। ਹੋਰ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਜੋੜ ਲੈਣ ਨਾਲ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਮਨ ਦੀ ਮਲਕੀਅਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣ ਜਾਂਦਾ, ਪਰ ਪੜ੍ਹਾਈ ਸਮਝ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਡੂੰਘਾ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Understand the limits of language without making ignorance a virtue.
study.closeReading: The opening line continues the poem’s comprehensive address through ਸਰਬ twice, then refuses confinement to a guise. The remaining three lines examine the means by which a reader might try to define that reality: teachings, revered books and the mind itself. ਨੇਤਿ interrupts the wish to identify one final description with the whole. The last line increases the imagined quantity of texts, yet still does not promise complete mental possession. This movement should not be used to excuse careless interpretation. On the contrary, recognising the limits of language gives the learner reason to distinguish what the words say, what a commentary proposes and what remains uncertain. The stanza closes the Rooaal sequence before the separate heading at 87.

words.workingGloss: going or reaching in this working reading
not confined to an outward guise
a refusal of final identification: not this, not that
a very large number; here an intensifier

study.interpretationCare: The limits of complete knowledge do not discredit education, evidence or reason. The explanation of ਨੇਤਿ is contextual and introductory, not a claim that all traditions use the term identically.
study.reflection: What is one place where you could study carefully while letting go of the need to sound certain about everything?
study.teachBack: Explain the progression from sacred teachings to the mind, and why the final line is not a command to stop reading.

simple.en: After the long Rooaal lines, the Madhubhaar heading brings a compact sequence of virtues, boundless greatness, an unbreakable seat and praise beyond comparison. Shorter lines still carry distinct images that deserve separate attention.
simple.pa: ਰੂਆਲ ਦੀਆਂ ਲੰਮੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਮਧੁਭਾਰ ਸਿਰਲੇਖ ਹੇਠ ਗੁਣਾਂ, ਬੇਅੰਤ ਮਹਿਮਾ, ਅਟੁੱਟ ਆਸਣ ਅਤੇ ਤੁਲਨਾ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਉਸਤਤ ਦੀਆਂ ਛੋਟੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਆਉਂਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਛੋਟੀਆਂ ਹੋਣ ਦੇ ਬਾਵਜੂਦ ਹਰ ਤੁਕ ਆਪਣਾ ਵੱਖਰਾ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਰੱਖਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Notice the change of form without losing the four separate images.
study.closeReading: The heading is separate from the four source lines and marks the transition to Madhubhaar. The first pair names virtues and then the impossibility of measuring greatness. The second pair offers a firm seat while again resisting a bounded comparison. That alternation matters: a concrete image such as a throne helps the imagination, but the next line prevents the image from becoming a complete definition. Read ਆਸਨ as imagery before assuming it is an instruction about the reader’s body. The final phrase also needs interpretive modesty; the beauty emphasis and the beyond-bodily-comparison reading should remain distinguishable. The form becomes compact, not simplistic.

words.workingGloss: an abundance or gathering of virtues
beyond bodily limitation in this provisional reading

study.interpretationCare: No human ruler inherits an unbreakable throne from this image. The final phrase remains a working interpretation, and the metrical heading receives no extra verse credit.
study.reflection: When an image helps you understand something, how do you remember that the image is not the whole reality?
study.teachBack: Identify the new metrical heading, explain why it is separate, and contrast the concrete seat image with the limits of comparison.

simple.en: Self-revealing light and enduring presence are followed by a heroic image and supreme sovereignty. The stanza shifts between descriptions beyond physical limits and an image drawn from bodily majesty without requiring the image to be literal anatomy.
simple.pa: ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਤੋਂ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਅਤੇ ਅਵਿਨਾਸ਼ੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਵੀਰਤਾ ਦਾ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਅਤੇ ਪਰਮ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹੀ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਛੰਦ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ ਦੇ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਨਾਲ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈ; ਇਸ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਾਬਦਿਕ ਸਰੀਰ ਮੰਨਣਾ ਲਾਜ਼ਮੀ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Hold the long-armed image beside the poem’s earlier freedom from bodily limits.
study.closeReading: The first two lines address the source of light and the persistence of the One through the changing cycle of night and day. The third changes the kind of language being used: far-reaching arms offer an image of majesty and capacity. Earlier lines have denied confinement to bodily limbs, so the image should be read within the whole poem rather than used to cancel those denials. The final sovereign title raises the scale beyond any individual ruler. A learner can therefore ask two different questions: what image is being offered, and what claim would go too far if the image were made literal? The distinction protects both the force of the poetry and honesty about interpretation.

words.workingGloss: self-revealing light in the selected reading
a traditional long-armed image of majesty

study.interpretationCare: No light vision, bodily characteristic or spiritual experience is required for a person to belong or practise. The different interpretations of ਅਨਭਉ and ਆਜਾਨ remain visible rather than being presented as settled.
study.reflection: Think of a metaphor that gives you courage. How could you keep its meaning without insisting it must describe a literal event?
study.teachBack: Explain why the arm image need not contradict earlier bodilessness language, and distinguish the sovereign title from a breath-related reading.

simple.en: Rulers, suns and gods become points of comparison, and each comparison points beyond itself. The final line gathers these images into praise rather than treating any finite authority, brilliance or heavenly power as the final limit.
simple.pa: ਰਾਜੇ, ਸੂਰਜ ਅਤੇ ਦੇਵਤੇ ਤੁਲਨਾ ਦੇ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਬਣਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਹਰ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਦੀ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਉਸਤਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੋੜਦੀ ਹੈ; ਕੋਈ ਸੀਮਤ ਸੱਤਾ, ਚਾਨਣ ਜਾਂ ਦੇਵਤਾ ਅੰਤਿਮ ਹੱਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਦਾ।

study.focus: Recognise the repeated pattern of surpassing comparison.
study.closeReading: The first three lines use a similar verbal construction while changing the comparison: political power, visible brilliance and heavenly authority. None is dismissed as an empty word, yet none is allowed to set the final scale. The fourth line names praise and greatness, making the function of the comparisons more apparent. This way of reading can help the learner avoid two extremes: reducing the lines to a literal ranking chart, or flattening all three into a vague statement that the Divine is great. Keep the distinct images first, then ask how each is exceeded. The result is a widening of reverence, not a warrant for human domination.

words.workingGloss: the Divine revered beyond the gods

study.interpretationCare: Solar language is poetic, not a scientific explanation. Political and divine titles do not confer absolute authority on any person, institution or state.
study.reflection: Which kind of human greatness most easily captures your attention—power, brilliance or reputation—and what helps you keep it in proportion?
study.teachBack: Name the three kinds of comparison and explain what the final line tells you about their purpose.

simple.en: The stanza reaches from heavenly sovereignty and exalted rank to the poorest person, then beyond death. Its change of direction matters: greatness is not confined to prestige, and the presence of the Divine is not measured by wealth.
simple.pa: ਛੰਦ ਦੇਵਤਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਰਾਜਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਉੱਚੇ ਮਾਣ ਤੋਂ ਗਰੀਬਾਂ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਗਰੀਬ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦਾ ਹੈ, ਫਿਰ ਕਾਲ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਮੋੜ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਹੈ: ਵਡਿਆਈ ਕੇਵਲ ਰੁਤਬੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੱਝੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਧਨ ਨਾਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਤੋਲੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ।

study.focus: Notice how the line about poverty interrupts a simple ladder of rank.
study.closeReading: The repeated construction might initially sound like a steady ascent through higher and higher titles. The third line disrupts that expectation with ਰੰਕਾਨ ਰੰਕ. The final line then goes beyond the ordinary categories of rank by addressing death itself. The second line also requires an explicit interpretive choice. This draft uses the exalted sense supported by the ਬਾਲਾ lexical comparison and the consulted commentary, while preserving the different smallness or child reading found elsewhere. Do not hide that difference behind a single polished sentence. Whatever reading receives eventual qualified approval, the poor must not disappear from the stanza. Reflection can attend to the dignity of someone with little social power while still recognising the hardship of deprivation.

words.workingGloss: higher than the highest in the selected reading; alternatives retained
beyond death or the death of death

study.interpretationCare: The ਬਾਲਾਨ ਬਾਲ reading needs qualified Sikh/Punjabi review. Poverty is not proof of virtue or fault, and it should not be romanticised. The final line promises no bodily immortality.
study.reflection: Who might be overlooked because they lack status or money, and what respectful, practical action would recognise their dignity?
study.teachBack: Explain the selected and alternative readings of the second line, then describe how the third line changes the direction of the stanza.

simple.en: The passage moves from freedom from an elemental body to enduring radiance, immeasurability and generosity. Its last line returns to a phrase already heard in Chhand 87. The return lets a familiar quality stand beside new descriptions without implying that a complete portrait of the Divine has been achieved.
simple.pa: ਇਸ ਛੰਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਪਦਾਰਥਕ ਸਰੀਰ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹਸਤੀ, ਅਟੁੱਟ ਜੋਤਿ, ਬੇਅੰਤ ਗਤਿ ਅਤੇ ਉਦਾਰ ਗੁਣ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਛੰਦ ੮੭ ਦੀ ਜਾਣੀ ਹੋਈ ਉਸਤਤ ਮੁੜ ਲਿਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਜਾਣਿਆ ਗੁਣ ਨਵੇਂ ਸੰਦਰਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਬਣ ਜਾਣ ਦਾ ਦਾਅਵਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦਾ।

study.focus: Notice what is denied, what is affirmed, and what returns from an earlier passage.
study.closeReading: Begin with the movement between the four lines. The first prevents the image of a body from becoming a boundary around the One. The second nevertheless permits a positive image: radiance that does not fragment. The third makes even the scale of that radiance impossible to finish measuring. The final line then returns to generous qualities rather than leaving the reader with abstraction alone. Its repetition from Chhand 87 is worth noticing; a repeated phrase can carry continuity without needing a new definition. In your own account, distinguish the words about elements and measure from the practical response of humility that you draw from them. The latter is an application, not another source line.

words.workingGloss: not constituted from material elements; working reading

study.interpretationCare: The traditional elemental vocabulary is not a chemistry lesson. Radiance is not an instruction to seek unusual visual experiences. The repeated earlier explanation is preserved rather than silently improved.
study.reflection: What changes when you describe something you value without assuming that your description exhausts it?
study.teachBack: Explain the four movements of this chhand and identify the phrase repeated from Chhand 87.

simple.en: Sages bow before a fear-free, desire-free reality whose radiance and wholeness exceed their descriptions. The stanza can be read beside Chhand 91: the paired words for ways and measure appear in reversed order, while the closing emphasis moves from boundlessness to unbroken completeness.
simple.pa: ਮੁਨੀ ਡਰ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਮਨਾ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਉਸ ਹਸਤੀ ਅੱਗੇ ਝੁਕਦੇ ਹਨ ਜਿਸ ਦਾ ਤੇਜ ਅਤੇ ਅਖੰਡਤਾ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਵਰਣਨ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੇ ਹਨ। ਛੰਦ ੯੧ ਨਾਲ ਪੜ੍ਹਨ ਤੇ ਗਤਿ ਅਤੇ ਮਿਤਿ ਦੇ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਉਲਟ ਕ੍ਰਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਦਿੱਸਦੇ ਹਨ। ਅਖੀਰਲਾ ਜ਼ੋਰ ਬੇਅੰਤਤਾ ਤੋਂ ਅਖੰਡਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Read reverence as a response to wholeness rather than a display of personal spiritual achievement.
study.closeReading: The opening places learned seekers in the position of bowing. Knowledge is present, but it is not presented as ownership of the One being praised. The next line joins freedom from fear with freedom from craving; neither is introduced as a command that a learner must instantly stop feeling. The third line turns toward brilliance, and the fourth toward an undivided reality. Compare ਗਤਿ ਮਿਤਿ in the preceding chhand with ਮਿਤਿ ਗਤਿ here. The change in order invites attention, but does not establish a technical doctrine on its own. A careful reading can notice the verbal pattern, retain the selected sense of wholeness, and leave alternative explanations visible for qualified review.
study.interpretationCare: Fear and need are normal human experiences. This praise neither diagnoses them as spiritual failure nor promises their clinical disappearance. Spellings are not normalised by the explanation.
study.reflection: Where could humility improve your use of knowledge without making you abandon careful inquiry?
study.teachBack: Describe the relationship between the sages, fearlessness, brilliance and wholeness; compare the final line with 91.03.

simple.en: This closing Madhubhaar passage holds effortless action, dharam, sustenance and freedom from punishment together. Several expressions admit more than one interpretation. The lesson selects a working reading while keeping the alternatives visible, rather than treating an uncertain gloss as a corrected original.
simple.pa: ਮਧੁਭਾਰ ਦੇ ਇਸ ਅਖੀਰਲੇ ਛੰਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਹਜ ਕਰਮ, ਧਰਮ, ਪਾਲਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਦੰਡ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੋਣਾ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਕੁਝ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਦੇ ਇੱਕ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਅਰਥ ਮਿਲਦੇ ਹਨ। ਇੱਥੇ ਚੁਣਿਆ ਅਰਥ ਸਮਝਣ ਲਈ ਹੈ; ਹੋਰ ਅਰਥ ਵੀ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹੇ ਰੱਖੇ ਹਨ ਅਤੇ ਮੂਲ ਪਾਠ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਦਲਿਆ ਗਿਆ।

study.focus: Keep a difficult working interpretation separate from a claim that the source has been settled.
study.closeReading: The first two lines resist an easy picture of the Divine as a larger version of a human worker. Action is named, yet ordinary strain and binding action are not simply transferred to the One. Dharam follows, with exemplary and unseen readings that need to remain distinguishable. The third line brings the discussion back to the sustaining of all, while its alternative ornament reading would highlight fullness differently. The last line denies punishment by a superior authority. Do not turn that final denial into a rule about human leaders. A sound teach-back names the selected interpretation, gives at least one genuine alternative, and explains why uncertainty about a gloss is not permission to alter the Gurmukhi.

words.workingGloss: exemplary; unseen is an attested alternative
abundant sustenance; ornament reading also recorded

study.interpretationCare: This is an openly provisional lesson. It neither excuses inaction nor places a human authority beyond scrutiny. The alternatives for dharam and adornment require qualified Sikh/Punjabi review.
study.reflection: How can you acknowledge that a word is difficult while still reading with attention rather than rushing past it?
study.teachBack: Explain the selected senses of all four lines, then state the alternative for ਆਦ੍ਰਿਸ੍ਯ and one limit of the lesson’s authority.

simple.en: At the new Chachari heading, four compact addresses gather sustenance, liberation, generosity and boundlessness. Each line offers a quality through which to turn toward the One. These names support attention without claiming to contain the whole reality they address.
simple.pa: ਨਵੀਂ ਚਾਚਰੀ ਸਿਰਲੇਖ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਚਾਰ ਛੋਟੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਪਾਲਣਾ, ਮੁਕਤੀ, ਉਦਾਰਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਬੇਅੰਤਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਇਕੱਠਾ ਕਰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ। ਹਰ ਤੁਕ ਇੱਕ ਗੁਣ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਮੋੜਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਨਾਮ ਉਸ ਹਸਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਘੇਰ ਲੈਣ ਦਾ ਦਾਅਵਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰਦੇ।

study.focus: Let four short addresses retain four distinct meanings.
study.closeReading: The change of heading is a change in the poem’s stated metrical setting, not an extra verse to count as teaching coverage. Read the four addresses in their sequence. Sustaining care comes first, then release, then generosity, and finally the refusal of a limit. These are related, but they are not interchangeable. A short word can carry a large field of meaning; the reader need not add an elaborate visualisation to make it significant. The next chhand will turn toward dissolution, making and the limits of names themselves. Keeping that next movement in view helps prevent any one title here from becoming a fixed boundary around the One.
study.interpretationCare: The heading remains a separate source record, not a fifth verse line. This silent reader provides no audio timing or authorised pronunciation lesson, and no numerical recitation benefit is promised.
study.reflection: Which of these four qualities invites a small act of care from you today, without making that act a transaction?
study.teachBack: Give one distinct meaning for each of the four addresses and explain why their brevity does not make them interchangeable.

simple.en: Ending and making are placed together before the poem denies a limiting name and self-seeking desire. Read after Chhand 94, this prevents the attractive names of generosity and liberation from becoming a narrow description. Reverence remains possible even when no name is exhaustive.
simple.pa: ਸਮੇਟਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਰਜਣਾ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ; ਫਿਰ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਅਤੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਲਈ ਕਾਮਨਾ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੋਣਾ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਛੰਦ ੯੪ ਨਾਲ ਪੜ੍ਹਿਆਂ ਇਹ ਗੱਲ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਦੀ ਹੈ ਕਿ ਉਦਾਰਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਦੇ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਨਾਮ ਵੀ ਪੂਰਾ ਵਰਣਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਹਨ। ਨਾਮ ਅਧੂਰਾ ਹੋ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਸੱਚੀ ਰਹਿ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Hold creation and dissolution together while noticing the limit placed on names.
study.closeReading: The first two lines form a pair: taking away and making. Do not make the first disappear merely because it is harder to receive. The third line then changes the question from what happens to how the One can be named. The many titles of the preceding passage have not been withdrawn, but they cannot become an exhaustive definition. The fourth line removes another familiar human explanation, craving for something one lacks. These movements offer a disciplined reading exercise: distinguish the two activities, the limit of naming, and freedom from self-seeking desire. Any reflection on change in one’s own life is an application of that reading, not a new claim about why a particular loss occurred.

words.workingGloss: taking away or dissolving; selected contextual sense

study.interpretationCare: Dissolution language does not explain away grief or make harm acceptable. No human being may claim Divine desirelessness as immunity from scrutiny. The source’s short words remain unchanged.
study.reflection: Can you acknowledge a change or ending without pretending to know its ultimate purpose?
study.teachBack: Explain the pairing of ਹਰੀਅੰ and ਕਰੀਅੰ, then describe how naming and desire are treated in the final two lines.

simple.en: The Bhujang Prayat heading begins a sequence built around the same four-directions phrase. Creation, dissolution, giving and knowing each receive that full scope. Repetition connects them while allowing each act to remain distinct; the phrase is not merely decorative.
simple.pa: ਭੁਜੰਗ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਤ ਸਿਰਲੇਖ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਇੱਕੋ ਚਾਰ ਦਿਸ਼ਾਵਾਂ ਵਾਲਾ ਵਾਕੰਸ਼ ਮੁੜ ਮੁੜ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਕਰਤਾਰੀ, ਸੰਘਾਰ, ਦਾਤ ਅਤੇ ਗਿਆਨ—ਚਾਰਾਂ ਦਾ ਵਿਸਥਾਰ ਹਰ ਪਾਸੇ ਹੈ। ਦੁਹਰਾਉਂਦੀ ਬੋਲੀ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਜੋੜਦੀ ਹੈ ਪਰ ਹਰ ਗੁਣ ਦੀ ਆਪਣੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਵੀ ਕਾਇਮ ਰੱਖਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Use the repeated phrase to hear the scope of four different predicates.
study.closeReading: Read each line by first noticing the common opening and then the changed final word. The pattern makes the differences easier to hear: creator, dissolver, giver, knower. Creation and dissolution repeat a pairing from the preceding chhand, but now their scope is made explicit through the directions. Giving and knowing complete the stanza rather than leaving the account at sheer power. In a careful explanation, all four words deserve attention. The stored forms of the repeated opening contain spelling features that differ from another witness; the teaching layer preserves them. Universal scope is a poetic and devotional claim here, not a geographic survey or a scientific measurement.

words.workingGloss: region or quarter in the repeated directional phrase
one who takes away or dissolves

study.interpretationCare: No direction, community or state is assigned ownership of Divine power. Giving is not a guarantee of wealth; dissolution does not excuse violence. Original spelling differences remain open.
study.reflection: Does recognising a wider field of concern change whom you include when offering practical help?
study.teachBack: Name the four changed final words and explain what the repeated opening contributes to each.

simple.en: Presence, filling, nurture and time share the same universal scope. The last line makes the stanza more demanding than a simple promise of comfort. The lesson keeps care and ending together without turning the passage into an explanation of anyone’s particular suffering.
simple.pa: ਵਿਆਪਕਤਾ, ਭਰਪੂਰਤਾ, ਪਾਲਣਾ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਲ—ਇਹ ਸਾਰੇ ਹਰ ਦਿਸ਼ਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਇਸ ਛੰਦ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਆਰਾਮ ਦੇ ਵਾਅਦੇ ਤੱਕ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਰਹਿਣ ਦਿੰਦੀ। ਇੱਥੇ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਤ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਰੱਖੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਕਿਸੇ ਖ਼ਾਸ ਦੁੱਖ ਦਾ ਕਾਰਨ ਨਹੀਂ ਘੜਿਆ ਗਿਆ।

study.focus: Do not erase the final time-and-ending line from a stanza about care.
study.closeReading: The first three lines can initially sound like a steady movement toward reassurance. Presence is everywhere; the expanse is filled or sustained; beings are cared for. The fourth line retains the same opening but changes the final quality to ਕਾਲੇ. That structural sameness asks the reader to hold a harder quality in the same act of praise. It does not require pretending that loss is easy or that one knows why it happened. Compare this stanza with 96: the shared opening continues, while the changed words form a new pattern. A good reading names both the continuity of scope and the difference between filling, nurture and ending.

words.workingGloss: time or the ending of forms

study.interpretationCare: Spiritual nurture does not replace practical care. The passage promises no immunity from illness or death and supplies no justification for treating loss as another person’s fault.
study.reflection: How might care remain real and valuable even when it cannot prevent every loss?
study.teachBack: Explain the first three qualities, then say why the last line must remain present in a summary.

simple.en: The directional sequence closes with nearness, dwelling, honour and giving. These words connect vastness with relationship. The One praised as present everywhere is not simply remote; yet the lesson does not promise that a person will always feel that nearness.
simple.pa: ਦਿਸ਼ਾਵਾਂ ਵਾਲੀ ਲੜੀ ਨੇੜਤਾ, ਵਾਸ, ਸਤਿਕਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਦਾਤ ਨਾਲ ਮੁੱਕਦੀ ਹੈ। ਇਹ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਵਿਸਥਾਰ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਬੰਧ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜਦੇ ਹਨ। ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਦੂਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਗਿਆ, ਪਰ ਇਸ ਤੋਂ ਇਹ ਵਾਅਦਾ ਵੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਦਾ ਕਿ ਮਨੁੱਖ ਹਰ ਵੇਲੇ ਉਹ ਨੇੜਤਾ ਮਹਿਸੂਸ ਕਰੇਗਾ।

study.focus: Distinguish nearness from dwelling and honour from giving.
study.closeReading: The common opening now supports relational words rather than the creation-and-dissolution pairing that began the sequence. Nearness and dwelling are related, but nearness addresses relation while dwelling addresses presence. Honour and giving then place response and generosity beside one another. The repeated directions prevent either from being restricted to a chosen corner of the world. Compare the closing giver here with the giver in 96; the return helps join the three chhands without making their whole contents identical. In reflection, one may ask how to offer attention across boundaries. That ethical application is not proof that every historical community interpreted the stanza in the same way.

words.workingGloss: near or beside; working contextual sense

study.interpretationCare: Devotional nearness is not a demand to feel comfort on command. The lesson does not rank communities by faith or treat the inability to feel consolation as wrongdoing.
study.reflection: What would it look like to offer respectful attention to someone outside your usual circle?
study.teachBack: Explain how this chhand completes the three-chhand directional sequence without repeating every quality from 96 and 97.

simple.en: After the expansive directional sequence, a new Chachari heading begins four negations: no enemy, no partisan friend, no delusion and no fear. These denials resist making the Divine a member of a human faction. They do not remove people’s need for friendship, safety or careful questioning.
simple.pa: ਵਿਸ਼ਾਲ ਦਿਸ਼ਾਵਾਂ ਵਾਲੀ ਲੜੀ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਨਵੀਂ ਚਾਚਰੀ ਚਾਰ ਨਕਾਰਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ: ਵੈਰੀ ਨਹੀਂ, ਪੱਖਪਾਤੀ ਮਿੱਤਰ ਨਹੀਂ, ਭਰਮ ਨਹੀਂ ਅਤੇ ਡਰ ਨਹੀਂ। ਇਹ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਧੜੇ ਦਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਤੋਂ ਰੋਕਦੇ ਹਨ। ਮਨੁੱਖ ਦੀ ਦੋਸਤੀ, ਸੁਰੱਖਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਸਵਾਲ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਮਿਟਦੀ।

study.focus: Read the repeated ਨ as a limit on projection, not a ban on human relationships.
study.closeReading: Every line starts by saying no. Rather than adding another image of power, the passage removes familiar constraints: rivalry, partial friendship, misconception and fear. The first pair is especially easy to misread when detached from the address. It does not command readers to abandon friends or stop resisting harm; it refuses to place the One inside those limited social roles. The last pair prevents ignorance and fear from explaining Divine action. The following chhands continue the same compact pattern of denial. Listen to that continuity while allowing each denied quality to remain specific. A practical application may examine one’s own partisanship, but it should not erase accountability or safe boundaries.
study.interpretationCare: Non-partisanship is not moral indifference. Nothing here instructs a person to remain with an abuser, reject friendship, or treat fear as a failure of faith.
study.reflection: Where can you distinguish a fair boundary from a need to label another person as an absolute enemy?
study.teachBack: Name all four negations and explain why the friend line is not an instruction to isolate yourself.

simple.en: The hundredth chhand continues the compact denials, turning toward karma, body and birth. Its final word has a recorded alternative concerning place. The lesson preserves the selected birthless reading and identifies the alternative instead of silently using one as if all commentators agreed.
simple.pa: ਸੌਵਾਂ ਛੰਦ ਛੋਟੇ ਨਕਾਰਾਂ ਦੀ ਲੜੀ ਨੂੰ ਕਰਮ, ਕਾਇਆ ਅਤੇ ਜਨਮ ਵੱਲ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ। ਅਖੀਰਲੇ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਲਈ ਥਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੋਣ ਦਾ ਹੋਰ ਅਰਥ ਵੀ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਅਜਨਮੇ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਰਥ ਚੁਣਿਆ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਅਰਥ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਾ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਹੈ; ਸਭ ਦੀ ਸਹਿਮਤੀ ਦਾ ਦਾਅਵਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ।

study.focus: Separate freedom from karma, freedom from bodily limitation and birthlessness.
study.closeReading: The first two lines keep the explicit ਨ, while the final two express denial through their own word forms. This gives the stanza continuity without requiring identical grammar in every line. Karma, body and birth are connected features of ordinary existence, yet each receives its own address. Read the last two lines slowly: a repetition of birthlessness can be meaningful, but the alternative place-related analysis of ਅਜਾਏ should not be hidden. The working choice is an editorial decision, not a correction of the source. In explaining the chhand to another person, retain that distinction and avoid turning descriptions of the Divine into promises of personal exemption from consequences or bodily needs.
study.interpretationCare: Spiritual reading does not excuse harmful conduct or replace bodily care. The alternative reading of the final word remains unresolved until qualified review; the draft is not santhiya authority.
study.reflection: How can responsibility for your actions coexist with humility about what lies beyond your complete understanding?
study.teachBack: Describe the three main limits denied here and state the two working analyses recorded for the final word.

simple.en: The stanza denies confinement to a portrait or a partial friendship, then affirms beyondness and purity. Its repeated friend line retains the earlier explanation. This balance of denial and affirmation helps the reader avoid turning either an image or a verbal definition into the whole of the Divine.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਅਤੇ ਪੱਖਪਾਤੀ ਮਿੱਤਰਤਾ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੋਣਾ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਫਿਰ ਪਰੇਪਣ ਅਤੇ ਪਵਿੱਤਰਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਮੰਨਦਾ ਹੈ। ਮਿੱਤਰ ਵਾਲੀ ਦੁਹਰਾਈ ਤੁਕ ਦਾ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਰਥ ਹੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਨਕਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਣ ਦੀ ਇਹ ਜੋੜੀ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਜਾਂ ਪਰਿਭਾਸ਼ਾ ਨੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਹਸਤੀ ਸਮਝ ਲੈਣ ਤੋਂ ਰੋਕਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Notice how the stanza moves from two denials to two affirmations.
study.closeReading: The first pair shares the opening ਨ, and the second pair changes the movement. A picture is not sufficient; a particular friendship does not define the One. Yet the passage does not stop at saying what cannot be said. Beyondness and purity remain affirmative ways of addressing the Divine. The friend line already appeared at 99.02, and preserving its explanation lets its changed setting do the interpretive work. Compare a statement about a picture’s limits with a statement that pictures have no value at all; these are not the same. Likewise, an application to fairness should not become an instruction to withdraw from friendship. Keep the subject of the praise in view.
study.interpretationCare: Neither friendship nor creativity is condemned by this draft. Purity must not be used to rank human bodies or social groups. Source-specific explanation is distinct from a ruling on religious practice.
study.reflection: Can a meaningful image or description help you without becoming something you mistake for the whole reality?
study.teachBack: Explain the shift from denial to affirmation and why the repeated friend line keeps the same main explanation.

simple.en: Earthly sovereignty is placed beside what sight cannot encompass and what cannot be diminished. The two central addresses have differing digital interpretations. This lesson makes its working unseen reading explicit, while leaving the discrepancy available for later qualified review.
simple.pa: ਧਰਤੀ ਦੀ ਸੁਆਮੀਤਾ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਉਹ ਹਸਤੀ ਦੱਸੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਜ਼ਰ ਘੇਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦੀ ਅਤੇ ਜਿਸ ਦੀ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਘਟਦੀ ਨਹੀਂ। ਵਿਚਕਾਰਲੇ ਦੋ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਲਈ ਡਿਜ਼ੀਟਲ ਅਰਥਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਹੈ। ਇੱਥੇ ਅਣਦਿਸ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਰਥ ਚੁਣਿਆ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਫ਼ਰਕ ਨੂੰ ਅੱਗੇ ਦੀ ਯੋਗ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਲਈ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਾ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Keep the chosen reading visible when two comparison columns do not agree.
study.closeReading: The first line gives a relational title, sovereign of the earth. The next two prevent that sovereignty from being reduced to an ordinary visible ruler. Their sound and sense overlap in the working reading, while the final line adds undiminished capacity. Do not invent a technical distinction merely to make every line different. Instead, acknowledge both the related meanings and the alternatives found in the comparison material. This is a useful example of reading with precision and restraint: retain the exact source words, say which sense is used, and decline to claim that disagreement has been settled. Its devotional movement remains intelligible without pretending that every lexical question has a final answer.

words.workingGloss: not visible; alternative rendering remains open

study.interpretationCare: A limitation of ordinary sight is not a demand to report a supernatural vision. Power language does not devalue weakness, illness or disability. Digital translation differences remain unresolved.
study.reflection: How could you distinguish careful uncertainty from careless guessing when explaining a difficult passage to someone else?
study.teachBack: Name the chosen four meanings and explain what remains uncertain in the two central lines.

simple.en: The Bhagvati heading introduces a fresh pattern in which each line begins with ਕਿ. Enduring realm, unbroken form, ongoing activity and the breaking of delusion are held together. Similar sounds do not mean identical functions: the last line moves from what cannot break to the breaking of misconception.
simple.pa: ਭਗਵਤੀ ਸਿਰਲੇਖ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਹਰ ਤੁਕ ਕਿ ਨਾਲ ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਅਟੱਲ ਦੇਸ, ਅਖੰਡ ਸਰੂਪ, ਅਮੁੱਕ ਕਰਮ ਅਤੇ ਭਰਮ ਤੋੜਨਾ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਮਿਲਦੀ ਧੁਨੀ ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਇੱਕੋ ਕੰਮ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦਾ: ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਨਾ ਟੁੱਟਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਤੋਂ ਭਰਮ ਤੋੜਨ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Follow the repeated opening while distinguishing endurance from the breaking of delusion.
study.closeReading: A separate heading signals the metrical transition; it is not counted as a fifth line. The repeated ਕਿ then links four short clauses. The first three concern what cannot be diminished, divided or defeated by another power. The final line introduces breaking in relation to ਭਰਮ, making a useful contrast with the surrounding language of unbrokenness. Similar-looking prefixes should not be forced into one automatic meaning. Attend to the whole phrase and retain the alternatives for the activity line. The working interpretation invites humility about one’s own misconceptions, but that application does not let a teacher claim that disagreement with the teacher is itself delusion.
study.interpretationCare: A metrical name does not by itself settle a theological identification. No human authority gains exemption from scrutiny through these descriptions. The interpretation and source spellings remain provisional and unchanged respectively.
study.reflection: What helps you reconsider a firmly held idea without replacing one unexamined certainty with another?
study.teachBack: Explain the four clauses, identify the separate heading, and describe the shift in the final line.

simple.en: The stanza joins non-attachment, the sun’s limits, purity and the origin of splendour. Its scale moves from worlds to a great light and then to descriptions of being and capacity. Genuine alternatives are retained for the first and third lines, without changing the original wording.
simple.pa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਨਿਰਲੇਪਤਾ, ਸੂਰਜ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ, ਪਵਿੱਤਰਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੋਭਾ ਦੇ ਮੂਲ ਨੂੰ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ। ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਦਾ ਵਿਸਥਾਰ, ਫਿਰ ਵੱਡੀ ਜੋਤਿ ਅਤੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਸਰੂਪ ਤੇ ਸਮਰੱਥਾ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਪਹਿਲੀ ਅਤੇ ਤੀਜੀ ਤੁਕ ਦੇ ਹੋਰ ਅਰਥ ਵੀ ਰੱਖੇ ਹਨ; ਮੂਲ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਦਲੇ।

study.focus: Read the sun image as a change of scale, not a prediction about an event.
study.closeReading: The first line has two significant interpretive possibilities: remaining unentangled in worlds, or a realm that remains unbroken. State the chosen one rather than concealing the choice. The sun in the second line then supplies a vivid example of a power that seems immense but is not ultimate. The next two clauses turn to purity and magnificence or capacity. This is a sequence of devotional addresses, not a report from an observatory. The exercise for a learner is to keep the concrete solar image while not converting it into a modern physical explanation. Similarly, the closing abundance language should remain visible without becoming a promised reward for spiritual practice.
study.interpretationCare: The solar line predicts no date or disaster. Non-attachment is not neglect of others, and abundance does not establish a method for obtaining wealth or powers. Qualified interpretation remains pending.
study.reflection: When something seems overwhelmingly powerful, what helps you acknowledge its limits without dismissing its real effects?
study.teachBack: State the alternative in the first line, explain the sun image, and distinguish the final abundance language from a promised personal reward.

simple.en: Radiance and a banner give public images to sovereignty and dharam, while freedom from sorrow and universal adornment close the stanza. The lesson distinguishes those images from claims about human rulers, visible wealth or a requirement to feel cheerful. The final word retains its adornment sense.
simple.pa: ਤੇਜ ਅਤੇ ਧੁਜਾ ਰਾਜ ਅਤੇ ਧਰਮ ਨੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਗਟ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਦਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ; ਸ਼ੋਕ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਸਰੂਪ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਦਾ ਸ਼ਿੰਗਾਰ ਛੰਦ ਨੂੰ ਮੁਕਾਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਹਾਕਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਮਨਜ਼ੂਰੀ, ਦੌਲਤ ਦੀ ਮਿਣਤੀ ਜਾਂ ਹਰ ਵੇਲੇ ਖ਼ੁਸ਼ ਰਹਿਣ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਾਇਆ ਗਿਆ। ਅਖੀਰਲੇ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਦਾ ਸ਼ਿੰਗਾਰ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਰਥ ਕਾਇਮ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Distinguish poetic signs of dharam from human claims to own it.
study.closeReading: The stanza begins with brightness associated with sovereignty and then shifts to a banner. Both images make something visible, but a visible sign is not the same as a guarantee that every bearer acts rightly. The third line changes the register toward the nature of the One, with a selected grief-free reading and a drying-or-burning alternative. The final line broadens adornment to all, rather than restricting splendour to a ruler or a costly object. In your own reflection, ask what an ethical sign points toward in conduct. Keep that practical question separate from translation: it is a response to the banner image, not an additional meaning smuggled into the Gurmukhi.

words.workingGloss: dharam; right order or righteous living
without sorrow; another analysis concerns drying

study.interpretationCare: A banner is not proof of a human group’s moral infallibility. Grief is not a failure of faith. The competing reading of ਆਸੋਕ remains explicit; no alteration to the source text is made.
study.reflection: What ordinary action would make a value you display visibly more trustworthy to the people around you?
study.teachBack: Explain the four images and distinguish the final adornment word from the nourishment reading discussed at Chhand 93.

simple.en: The address joins the making of the world, protection, the all-pervading Reality and incomparable spiritual knowing. Each description adds a different emphasis; none makes the Divine a limited human figure.
simple.pa: ਇਸ ਛੰਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਗਤ ਦੀ ਰਚਨਾ, ਰੱਖਿਆ, ਸਰਬ-ਵਿਆਪਕ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਅਤੇ ਬੇਮਿਸਾਲ ਅੰਦਰਲੀ ਸੂਝ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਹੈ। ਹਰ ਤੁਕ ਇੱਕ ਵੱਖਰਾ ਪੱਖ ਖੋਲ੍ਹਦੀ ਹੈ; ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਸੀਮਤ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੰਨ੍ਹਦੀ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Let creation, protection, pervasion and knowing remain four distinct descriptions.
study.closeReading: The repeated ਕਿ continues the address from the preceding chhands. First the world is spoken of as made; then the language turns toward protection. The canopy or warrior image can suggest shelter and strength without becoming a portrait of a human ruler. The third line widens the address again through ਬ੍ਰਹਮੰ, while the fourth brings attention to knowing and incomparability. Reading all four in sequence prevents one familiar image from taking over the stanza. The selected awareness reading of ਅਨਭਉ is provisional, with fearlessness kept visible as an alternative. For study, ask what each phrase contributes rather than reducing all four to a single statement that the Divine is great.

words.workingGloss: supreme protector; canopy and warrior images also occur

study.interpretationCare: The protector image is not a promise that faithful people cannot be hurt, nor authority for a human ruler to act without accountability. The two readings of ਅਨਭਉ need qualified review.
study.reflection: What would protection look like in a small action that respects another person’s dignity?
study.teachBack: Explain the four descriptions separately, then name one alternative reading without treating it as a corrected source word.

simple.en: The One is praised as primal, without a higher master, beyond full disclosure and beyond a fixed portrait. The closing phrase raises the relationship between Divine independence and the dependence of everything else.
simple.pa: ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਆਦਿ ਤੋਂ ਮੌਜੂਦ, ਕਿਸੇ ਹੋਰ ਦੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਨਾ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲਾ, ਅਥਾਹ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਸ਼ਚਿਤ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਆਖਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ। ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਸੁਤੰਤਰਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਰੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦੇ ਉਸ ਉੱਤੇ ਆਧਾਰ ਵੱਲ ਧਿਆਨ ਲਿਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Recognise limits on description without turning mystery into an excuse to stop learning.
study.closeReading: The first line places no superior above the One. The next two lines limit what a description can claim: the full ਭੇਵ is not possessed, and a ਚਿੱਤ੍ਰ cannot contain its subject. The last line can be read as dependence on the One alone or as the One’s own self-dependence. Keep this grammatical question open instead of hiding it inside a fluent paraphrase. Notice that the stanza still speaks, even while naming the limits of speech and images. That tension offers a useful learning posture: study carefully, say what a reading supports, and remain willing to revise an explanation. The unknowable is not permission for a teacher to demand unquestioning trust.
study.interpretationCare: Working interpretations are not settled grammar. Divine self-sufficiency should not become a demand that people avoid help, relationships or care.
study.reflection: Where can you say “I do not fully understand” while still staying curious and responsible?
study.teachBack: Contrast a useful description with a complete definition, and explain the two directions in which the closing dependence phrase is read.

simple.en: Daily sustenance and mercy stand beside purity and the hidden mystery of the Divine. The passage brings the ordinary need for livelihood into the same address as what remains beyond our knowledge.
simple.pa: ਰੋਜ਼ੀ ਅਤੇ ਰਹਿਮ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਪਵਿਤ੍ਰਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਅਥਾਹ ਗੁਪਤ ਭੇਦ ਦੀ ਉਸਤਤ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਡੀ ਸਮਝ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਰਹਿੰਦੀ ਹਸਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕੋ ਸੰਬੋਧਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਜੋੜਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Hold daily need, mercy, purity and mystery together without erasing their differences.
study.closeReading: The stanza starts close to ordinary life with ਰੋਜ਼ੀ, the means by which one lives. It then speaks of mercy, purity and a hiddenness beyond hiddenness. This movement matters: mystery is not placed outside everyday dependence. The paired terms in the first and third lines make different kinds of relationships, provider and provision in one, two reinforcing qualities in the other. The second line requires special care because ਰਿਹਾਕੈ has competing explanations. The main draft chooses release but keeps the vitality reading visible. An honest explanation can offer a working understanding while naming its limit. The final intensification invites humility, not the claim that a particular interpreter has discovered the whole secret.
study.interpretationCare: The ਰਿਹਾਕੈ choice remains unapproved. Provision language must never be used to blame poverty or replace feeding and supporting people in need.
study.reflection: What ordinary support have you received today, and how might gratitude become a practical act of sharing?
study.teachBack: Explain how provision and mystery share one stanza, and identify precisely which word has an unresolved alternative.

simple.en: Forgiveness, sovereignty, agency and daily provision appear in four brief addresses. The language of kings is placed next to mercy and food, inviting attention to the character of power rather than rank alone.
simple.pa: ਖਿਮਾ, ਸਰਬੋਚ ਸੱਤਾ, ਕਰਤਾਪਣ ਅਤੇ ਰੋਜ਼ੀ—ਇਹ ਚਾਰ ਪੱਖ ਛੋਟੀਆਂ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਸ਼ਾਹਾਂ ਵਾਲੀ ਬੋਲੀ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਰਹਿਮ ਅਤੇ ਰੋਜ਼ਾਨਾ ਜੀਵਨ ਦਾ ਆਸਰਾ ਵੀ ਹੈ; ਧਿਆਨ ਕੇਵਲ ਦਰਜੇ ਉੱਤੇ ਨਹੀਂ, ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਦੇ ਸੁਭਾਅ ਉੱਤੇ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Read sovereignty alongside forgiveness and provision, not as power isolated from care.
study.closeReading: The opening phrase concerns wrongdoing and pardon rather than abstract greatness. The second line then moves to the highest image of worldly rank, only to be followed by the doer of causes and the giver of daily sustenance. Look at how the sequence refuses to leave power as a title. The same addressed One is connected with mercy and the conditions of life. The last line also recalls the livelihood language in Chhand 108, so the link between neighbouring stanzas remains audible. In applying the lesson, distinguish acknowledging dependence from evading responsibility. One can seek forgiveness while also naming harm, making amends and avoiding a claim that Divine agency excuses personal decisions.
study.interpretationCare: Prayer for forgiveness does not compel another person to reconcile or excuse abuse. The sovereign title confers no political authority on the learner.
study.reflection: What could genuine accountability add to an apology that words alone cannot provide?
study.teachBack: Explain the sequence from pardon to daily provision, and distinguish forgiveness from denial of consequences.

simple.en: The provider is merciful and generous, yet the stanza also speaks of complete power and dissolution. The gentle and formidable descriptions belong to the same address; neither should be removed merely because it is less comfortable.
simple.pa: ਰੋਜ਼ੀ ਦੇਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਰਹਿਮਵਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਆਖਿਆ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਘਾਰ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਹੈ। ਕੋਮਲ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਚੰਡ ਦੋਵੇਂ ਪੱਖ ਇੱਕੋ ਉਸਤਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਨ; ਅਸੁਖਾਵੇਂ ਲੱਗਣ ਕਰਕੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਪੱਖ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਟਾਉਣਾ ਠੀਕ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Keep compassion and the ending of finite forms within the same reading.
study.closeReading: The first two lines bring back familiar words of provision and mercy. The final two broaden the scope to all power and the breaking of what is made. Notice the shift without explaining away either side. If the stanza is read only as comfort, ਦਲੀ disappears; if it is read only as domination, ਰਹੀਮ and ਕਰੀਮ disappear. The repeated address holds them together. This is also a useful place to practise contextual vocabulary: ਕਰਮ in a grace-filled pair should not mechanically repeat every earlier action-related explanation. The lesson invites care in interpretation, not a theory that tells us why a particular loss occurred. Practical compassion remains necessary when someone faces change or grief.

words.workingGloss: fullness of power in this reading

study.interpretationCare: Do not present bereavement as deserved, infer a Divine reason for a specific tragedy, or turn descriptions of overwhelming power into human entitlement.
study.reflection: How might you acknowledge a difficult change without either denying the loss or abandoning kindness?
study.teachBack: Describe the change of emphasis between the first and second pairs, and explain why neither pair should replace the other.

simple.en: The repeated word for everywhere links honour, giving, movement and dwelling. The address refuses to confine the Divine to one place, while keeping each of these relationships distinct.
simple.pa: ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਲਈ ਵਰਤਿਆ ਸਰਬੱਤ੍ਰ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਮਾਨ, ਦਾਨ, ਪਹੁੰਚ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਵਾਸ ਨੂੰ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ। ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਥਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ, ਪਰ ਹਰ ਤੁਕ ਦਾ ਵੱਖਰਾ ਪੱਖ ਵੀ ਕਾਇਮ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Notice how the same universal scope accompanies four different relationships.
study.closeReading: Each line repeats ਕਿ ਸਰਬੱਤ੍ਰ, creating a common frame before the final word changes. Read the changing words slowly: honour, giving, going and dwelling. This helps prevent the universal phrase from making all four lines sound interchangeable. The last pair is especially useful for study because movement and dwelling usually describe different human situations. Here both extend the address beyond a single location. The language can invite reverence wherever life is encountered, without requiring that every person articulate that reverence identically. A practical application is to question why kindness or respect would be reserved for one familiar setting. That application grows from reflection; it is not a fifth translated line.
study.interpretationCare: The universal devotional language does not erase differences between people or justify coercing agreement. Movement is a poetic description, not a scientific mechanism.
study.reflection: Is there an unfamiliar place or community where your ordinary respect becomes less consistent?
study.teachBack: Name the four changing ideas after ਸਰਬੱਤ੍ਰ and explain why going and dwelling can both belong in the address.

simple.en: Countries, appearances, shining presence and creation are gathered under the word everywhere. Divine presence is not confined to one territory or outward costume, and the stanza ends with the making of all.
simple.pa: ਦੇਸ, ਭੇਸ, ਬਿਰਾਜਮਾਨਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਰਚਨਾ—ਸਭ ਲਈ ਸਰਬੱਤ੍ਰ ਵਰਤਿਆ ਹੈ। ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਧਰਤੀ ਜਾਂ ਬਾਹਰਲੇ ਪਹਿਰਾਵੇ ਤੱਕ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ; ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਸਾਰੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਦੇ ਸਿਰਜਣਹਾਰ ਵੱਲ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Distinguish territory and appearance from the presence and making praised within them.
study.closeReading: The first two lines offer a pair that will return later: ਦੇਸੈ and ਭੇਸੈ. One concerns where, the other how something appears. The next two shift from those settings to radiant presence and creative activity. The rhyme of ਦੇਸੈ and ਭੇਸੈ is not a reason to give them one definition, just as ਰਾਜੈ and ਸਾਜੈ carry different meanings despite their shared sound. When the pair returns at Chhands 114 and 117, its main wording stays constant; new neighbours change the larger discussion, not the source phrase itself. This makes repetition a learning aid. One can recognise the familiar words and then ask what the next pair adds.

words.workingGloss: shining or abiding; reigning is another sense

study.interpretationCare: The selected sense of ਰਾਜੈ is provisional. Presence in every form does not require ignoring harmful conduct or endorsing every claim to leadership.
study.reflection: How might respect for a person survive a difference in dress, language or nationality?
study.teachBack: Explain the two rhyming pairs without making their meanings identical, and identify which pair will return later.

simple.en: Giving and receiving are placed beside majesty and radiance. The first pair has a genuine alternative reading involving dharam and indwelling, so the lesson names its selected interpretation rather than hiding the uncertainty.
simple.pa: ਦੇਣ ਅਤੇ ਲੈਣ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੁਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਹੈ। ਪਹਿਲੀਆਂ ਦੋ ਤੁਕਾਂ ਲਈ ਧਰਮ ਅਤੇ ਲੀਨ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੋਰ ਅਰਥ ਵੀ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ; ਇਸ ਲਈ ਚੁਣਿਆ ਅਰਥ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ, ਅਨਿਸ਼ਚਿਤਤਾ ਲੁਕਾਈ ਨਹੀਂ ਗਈ।

study.focus: Learn to state a selected reading and its alternative without mixing them into false certainty.
study.closeReading: This stanza provides a concrete exercise in honest interpretation. Reading ਦੀਨੈ and ਲੀਨੈ as giving and receiving makes the opening a paired movement. Reading them as dharam and indwelling instead joins a religious term with presence. These are not simply different English synonyms. The main draft follows the first pair while exposing the second in the expanded notes. The final two lines then praise majesty and radiance, so neither alternative should cause the rest of the stanza to disappear. A learner can understand the structure of both possibilities without deciding the source edition or grammar. Notice also that receiving back need not imply a human right to take from others; the addressee remains the Divine.

words.workingGloss: giving in the selected reading; deen/dharam is an alternative
taking or receiving here; indwelling is an alternative

study.interpretationCare: The first pair remains a qualified-review question. Do not turn giving-and-taking imagery into an explanation of a particular person’s loss or a justification for withholding help.
study.reflection: When two interpretations are plausible, what can you understand responsibly before choosing between them?
study.teachBack: Present both readings of the opening pair, say which this draft uses, and explain the two closing images.

simple.en: The familiar pair of every land and every form now leads into time or death and nurture. Repetition allows the same language of presence to frame both the ending of finite life and its care.
simple.pa: ਹਰ ਦੇਸ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਭੇਸ ਵਾਲੀ ਜਾਣੀ-ਪਛਾਣੀ ਜੋੜੀ ਇੱਥੇ ਕਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਵੱਲ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਉਹੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਦੀ ਬੋਲੀ ਸੀਮਤ ਜੀਵਨ ਦੇ ਅੰਤ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਦੋਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਘੇਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Hear the repeated opening while noticing the new relationship between ending and nurture.
study.closeReading: The first two lines have already appeared in Chhand 112. Their repetition establishes continuity rather than a new definition of ਦੇਸ or ਭੇਸ. What changes is the next pair: ਕਾਲੈ and ਪਾਲੈ. Their near-rhyme brings ending and nurture close together in sound, yet their meanings remain sharply different. Try reading the familiar pair first and then pausing before this new pair. The effect is not to solve the problem of suffering but to broaden the address beyond either comfort alone or destruction alone. For practical reflection, care for a living person remains meaningful even though life is finite. That application should be offered gently, never as a formula imposed on someone in grief.

words.workingGloss: every outward form, as in Chhand 112

study.interpretationCare: Nothing here warrants blaming grief or illness on spiritual failure. The repeated lines preserve their earlier meanings; the changed context is explained in Study.
study.reflection: How can awareness of life’s limits deepen practical care without turning into resignation?
study.teachBack: Identify the exact repeated opening pair and explain the contrast introduced by ਕਾਲੈ and ਪਾਲੈ.

simple.en: Dissolution, reaching everywhere, diverse appearances and seeing all are brought into one address. The stanza moves from overwhelming power to the breadth of presence and awareness without giving that power to a human observer.
simple.pa: ਸੰਘਾਰ, ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਪਹੁੰਚ, ਅਨੇਕ ਭੇਖ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਵੇਖਣਾ ਇੱਕੋ ਸੰਬੋਧਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ। ਪ੍ਰਚੰਡ ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਤੋਂ ਗੱਲ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਸੂਝ ਵੱਲ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ; ਇਹ ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਕਿਸੇ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਵੇਖਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਨੂੰ ਨਹੀਂ ਸੌਂਪੀ ਜਾਂਦੀ।

study.focus: Distinguish the forms encountered from the seeing that encompasses them.
study.closeReading: The repeated universal phrase is followed by four different endings. The first has a severe sense, the second speaks of reach, and the last pair brings form and seeing into relation. Read ਭੇਖੀ and ਪੇਖੀ together: their similar sound draws attention to a difference between appearance and awareness. The working movement sense of ਗੰਤਾ makes a transition from dissolving power to a reach that is not local; the knowing alternative would shift that transition toward awareness. Naming this choice is more useful than pretending the vocabulary has no uncertainty. Practical study can then ask how quickly we judge by clothing or role, without claiming that a person can acquire the Divine’s all-encompassing sight.

words.workingGloss: destroyer; the one who brings an end
going or reaching in this reading

study.interpretationCare: Dissolution is not an instruction to violence. All-seeing praise does not authorise intrusion into another person’s privacy or make a human teacher infallible.
study.reflection: What assumption about someone’s character have you made from their outward appearance that deserves a second look?
study.teachBack: Explain the four endings, then describe how ਭੇਖੀ and ਪੇਖੀ relate without giving them the same meaning.

simple.en: Activity and shining presence lead into a contrast between drying away and nourishing. The stanza keeps making, presence, decline and care within the same universal address, without converting those images into predictions about individual events.
simple.pa: ਕਾਰਜ ਅਤੇ ਬਿਰਾਜਮਾਨਤਾ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਸੁਕਾਉਣ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਲਣ ਦੀ ਜੋੜੀ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਕੰਮ, ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ, ਅੰਤ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਇੱਕੋ ਸਰਬ-ਵਿਆਪਕ ਸੰਬੋਧਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਨ; ਇਹ ਕਿਸੇ ਖ਼ਾਸ ਘਟਨਾ ਬਾਰੇ ਭਵਿੱਖਬਾਣੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਦੇ।

study.focus: Attend to the contrast in ਸੋਖੈ and ਪੋਖੈ rather than smoothing it into one pleasant idea.
study.closeReading: The first half speaks of activity and presence. The second half brings a sharper contrast: drying or dissolution, followed by nurture. Sound helps connect the lines, but it does not cancel their difference. Read the pair aloud silently in your mind and identify the distinct image in each. The returning ਰਾਜੈ line keeps its established main explanation from Chhand 112, now surrounded by another set of relationships. One useful learning habit is to recognise repeated wording without forcing all repeated passages into identical summaries. Reflection may connect the passage with the impermanence of what we care for, but it should not claim to explain a particular person’s suffering or prescribe indifference to it.

words.workingGloss: shining or abiding presence; reigning is an alternative

study.interpretationCare: No inference about the moral worth of someone experiencing loss follows from these images. Preservation of a repeated explanation is deliberate, not missing new content.
study.reflection: What can you care for today even though you cannot ensure that it will remain unchanged?
study.teachBack: Distinguish the two closing verbs, and explain how the repeated ਰਾਜੈ line gains context without changing its main meaning.

simple.en: Protection or strength is paired with life-breath, followed by the familiar language of every land and every form. The stanza links what sustains life with a presence that is not restricted by location or appearance.
simple.pa: ਤ੍ਰਾਣ ਜਾਂ ਬਲ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਪ੍ਰਾਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ ਫਿਰ ਹਰ ਦੇਸ ਤੇ ਹਰ ਭੇਸ ਵਾਲੀ ਜਾਣੀ ਜੋੜੀ ਆਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਜੀਵਨ ਦੇ ਆਸਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਅਜਿਹੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜਿਆ ਹੈ ਜੋ ਥਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਬਾਹਰਲੇ ਰੂਪ ਨਾਲ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: Link the first pair about sustaining life with the repeated pair about universal presence.
study.closeReading: The closeness in sound between ਤ੍ਰਾਣੈ and ਪ੍ਰਾਣੈ gives the first two lines their own relationship. Protection or strength is not the same word as life, though each can help illuminate the other. The second pair returns to ਦੇਸੈ and ਭੇਸੈ, which appeared in Chhands 112 and 114. This creates a small network of repetitions across the reading. Rather than treating the repetition as wasted space, use it to compare what surrounds it: creation in one stanza, time and nurture in another, and protection and life here. The reading stays anchored to the exact source lines. A personal application about care is offered separately from their wording, so it does not become a substitute translation.
study.interpretationCare: Life-breath vocabulary is devotional here, not a clinical claim or breathing prescription. A need for assistance is not a sign of spiritual failure.
study.reflection: Who or what helps sustain your daily life, and what would acknowledging that dependence change in your conduct?
study.teachBack: Distinguish ਤ੍ਰਾਣੈ from ਪ੍ਰਾਣੈ, then compare the repeated closing pair with its earlier settings.

simple.en: Universal honour leads to enduring primacy, remembrance and establishment. The stanza connects reverence with steadiness, while leaving open the interpretive range of what it means for the Divine to be remembered or made manifest everywhere.
simple.pa: ਸਭ ਥਾਂ ਮਾਨ ਤੋਂ ਗੱਲ ਸਦਾ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਧਾਨਤਾ, ਜਾਪ ਅਤੇ ਸਥਾਪਨਾ ਵੱਲ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ। ਅਦਬ ਅਤੇ ਟਿਕਾਅ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਹਨ; ਜਾਪਿਯੈ ਦੇ ਸਿਮਰਨ ਜਾਂ ਪ੍ਰਗਟ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਅਰਥ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਨੂੰ ਖੁੱਲ੍ਹਾ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਗਿਆ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Notice how the time-word ਸਦੈਵੰ changes a sequence dominated by everywhere.
study.closeReading: Three of the lines repeat the everywhere formula, but the second uses ਸਦੈਵੰ, always.
