jaap|jaap151.line02.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਸੁਹੱਪਣ ਦਾ ਚਾਨਣ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਦੀਵਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap151.line02.interpretiveCaution: The lamp is an image of beauty made radiant.

jaap|jaap151.line03.simpleEn: Your generosity is perfect and complete.
jaap|jaap151.line03.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਪੂਰਨ ਅਤੇ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap151.line03.interpretiveCaution: Kaamal and kareem join completeness with generosity.

jaap|jaap151.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਰਹਿਮ ਨਾਲ ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਜ਼ੀ ਅਤੇ ਆਸਰਾ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap151.line04.interpretiveCaution: Exact source repetition preserves the earlier provision-and-mercy wording.

jaap|jaap152.line01.simpleEn: You give the sustenance of each day.
jaap|jaap152.line01.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਹਰ ਦਿਨ ਦੀ ਰੋਜ਼ੀ ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap152.line01.interpretiveCaution: Rozi is daily provision; dihind names giving.

jaap|jaap152.line02.simpleEn: You sustain and set beings free.
jaap|jaap152.line02.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਾਲਣਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਮੁਕਤੀ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap152.line02.interpretiveCaution: Rahind is read through release; a continuing-sustainer sense is also recorded in commentary.

jaap|jaap152.line04.simpleEn: You are beauty in its fullness.
jaap|jaap152.line04.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਪੂਰਨ ਸੁਹੱਪਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap152.line04.interpretiveCaution: Husn and jamaal intensify the language of beauty.

jaap|jaap153.line01.simpleEn: Even hostile powers yield tribute to You.
jaap|jaap153.line01.simplePa: ਵੈਰੀ ਸ਼ਕਤੀਆਂ ਵੀ ਤੇਰੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਖ਼ਿਰਾਜ ਦਿੰਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ।
jaap|jaap153.line01.interpretiveCaution: This exact line retains the chhand 124 tribute reading.

jaap|jaap153.line02.simpleEn: You graciously lift up the poor.
jaap|jaap153.line02.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਗ਼ਰੀਬਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਹਰ ਨਾਲ ਉਚਾ ਚੁੱਕਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap153.line02.interpretiveCaution: Gareebul nivaaz specifically names gracious care for the poor.

jaap|jaap153.line03.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਵੈਰੀ ਦੀ ਵਿਰੋਧੀ ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਭੰਨਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap153.line03.interpretiveCaution: Shikann supplies the force of breaking opposition.

jaap|jaap153.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਡਰ ਨੂੰ ਦੂਰ ਸੁੱਟਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap153.line04.interpretiveCaution: Hiraas is fear; fikann supplies casting away.

jaap|jaap154.line01.simpleEn: You remove the stain of wrongdoing.
jaap|jaap154.line01.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਬੁਰਾਈ ਦੇ ਕਲੰਕ ਨੂੰ ਮਿਟਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap154.line01.interpretiveCaution: Kalank means stain or disgrace; the paraphrase follows its moral sense.

jaap|jaap154.line02.interpretiveCaution: Nivaas explicitly locates the Divine within all.

jaap|jaap154.line03.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਵੈਰੀ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਜਿੱਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap154.line03.interpretiveCaution: Aganj denies defeat by the ganeem, the enemy.

jaap|jaap154.line04.simpleEn: You are the merciful giver of sustenance.
jaap|jaap154.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਮਿਹਰਬਾਨ ਰੋਜ਼ੀ ਦੇਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap154.line04.interpretiveCaution: Razaaik is read as provider; mercy completes the epithet.

jaap|jaap155.line01.simpleEn: You are the power of speech in every tongue.
jaap|jaap155.line01.simplePa: ਹਰ ਜ਼ਬਾਨ ਦੀ ਬੋਲਣ-ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੂੰ ਮੌਜੂਦ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap155.line01.interpretiveCaution: Jubaan is tongue or language; the phrase embraces all speech.

jaap|jaap155.line02.simpleEn: You possess supreme and glorious sovereignty.
jaap|jaap155.line02.simplePa: ਸਰਬੋਤਮ ਅਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਤਾਪੀ ਬਾਦਸ਼ਾਹੀ ਤੇਰੀ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap155.line02.interpretiveCaution: Saahib-qiraan is an exalted sovereignty title; its historical image is explained in the study.

jaap|jaap155.line03.simpleEn: You bring hell to an end.
jaap|jaap155.line03.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਨਰਕ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap155.line03.interpretiveCaution: This repeats the exact hell-destroying line from chhand 130.

jaap|jaap155.line04.simpleEn: You dwell in the blessed realm of heaven.
jaap|jaap155.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਬਹਿਸ਼ਤ ਦੇ ਸੁਖਮਈ ਲੋਕ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap155.line04.interpretiveCaution: Bahisht is the Persian word for heaven; the line retains that religious image.

jaap|jaap156.line01.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਤੱਕ ਪਹੁੰਚਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap156.line01.interpretiveCaution: Gavann supplies going or reaching everywhere.

jaap|jaap156.line02.simpleEn: You are ever moving throughout creation.
jaap|jaap156.line02.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਸਦਾ ਸਾਰੀ ਰਚਨਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਚਰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap156.line02.interpretiveCaution: Ravann is read as continually moving or pervading; this is not an alteration of the source spelling.

jaap|jaap156.line03.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਸੂਝ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਹੈਂ।

jaap|jaap157.line01.simpleEn: You are sovereign even over the highest powers.
jaap|jaap157.line01.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਉੱਚੀਆਂ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਕਤੀਆਂ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਮਾਲਕ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap157.line01.interpretiveCaution: Param ees states sovereignty beyond the highest lords.

jaap|jaap157.line02.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਸਾਰਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਦ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਤੋਂ ਅਦਿੱਖ ਹੈਂ।

jaap|jaap157.line03.simpleEn: No land or written account can contain You.
jaap|jaap157.line03.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਦੇਸ਼ ਜਾਂ ਲਿਖਿਆ ਲੇਖਾ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap157.line03.interpretiveCaution: Adesul is read as beyond territorial limitation; alekh also recalls the limits of reckoning.

jaap|jaap157.line04.simpleEn: You are forever beyond any confining garb.
jaap|jaap157.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਸਦਾ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਭੇਖ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap157.line04.interpretiveCaution: Abhekh denies confinement in a particular outer appearance.

jaap|jaap158.line01.simpleEn: You pervade the earth and all time.
jaap|jaap158.line01.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਧਰਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap158.line01.interpretiveCaution: Earth and time is the selected reading; earth and heavens is another traditional rendering.

jaap|jaap158.line02.simpleEn: Your steadfast truth is profound beyond measure.
jaap|jaap158.line02.simplePa: ਤੇਰੇ ਧਰਮ ਅਤੇ ਅਟੱਲ ਸੱਚ ਦੀ ਗਹਿਰਾਈ ਅਥਾਹ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap158.line02.interpretiveCaution: The Mahan Kosh imaan entry specifically cites this line and supports the deep-dharam reading; signs is an alternative.

jaap|jaap158.line03.interpretiveCaution: This exact line retains the generosity wording from chhand 152.

jaap|jaap158.line04.simpleEn: Courage and beauty shine together in You.
jaap|jaap158.line04.simplePa: ਤੇਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਲੇਰੀ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਹੱਪਣ ਇਕੱਠੇ ਚਮਕਦੇ ਹਨ।
jaap|jaap158.line04.interpretiveCaution: Jurat and jamaal deliberately bring courage and beauty together.

jaap|jaap159.line01.simpleEn: Your light remains steady and unshaken.
jaap|jaap159.line01.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਸਦਾ ਅਡੋਲ ਰਹਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap159.line01.interpretiveCaution: Achal keeps the radiance steady rather than fleeting.

jaap|jaap159.line02.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਸੁਗੰਧ ਦੀ ਕੋਈ ਹੱਦ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap159.line02.interpretiveCaution: Subaas evokes fragrance as devotional imagery.

jaap|jaap159.line03.simpleEn: Your being is a wonder beyond telling.
jaap|jaap159.line03.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਬਿਆਨ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਅਚਰਜ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap159.line03.interpretiveCaution: Ajab voices wonder before the Divine form.

jaap|jaap159.line04.simpleEn: Your glory and abundance are immeasurable.
jaap|jaap159.line04.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਵਿਭੂਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਮਾਪ ਨਹੀਂ।

jaap|jaap160.line01.simplePa: ਤੇਰੇ ਪਸਾਰੇ ਦਾ ਕੋਈ ਮਾਪ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap160.line01.interpretiveCaution: Pasaa is read as expanse; grace or favour is another lexical possibility.

jaap|jaap160.line02.simpleEn: Your radiance shines from Your own being.
jaap|jaap160.line02.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਪ੍ਰਭਾ ਤੇਰੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਸਰੂਪ ਤੋਂ ਪ੍ਰਗਟ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap160.line02.interpretiveCaution: Aatam prabha is read as radiance arising from the Divine being itself.

jaap|jaap160.line03.simpleEn: You are unshaken and without bodily limitation.
jaap|jaap160.line03.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਅਡੋਲ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਸਰੀਰ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap160.line03.interpretiveCaution: Achal and anang join steadiness with freedom from bodily limits.

jaap|jaap160.line04.simpleEn: You are limitless and can never be broken.
jaap|jaap160.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਕਦੇ ਖੰਡਿਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦਾ।
jaap|jaap160.line04.interpretiveCaution: Amito and abhang join limitlessness with indestructibility.

jaap|jaap161.line01.simpleEn: Sages bow to You within their minds.
jaap|jaap161.line01.simplePa: ਰਿਸ਼ੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਮਨ ਤੇਰੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਨਿਵਦੇ ਹਨ।
jaap|jaap161.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਮੁਨਿ names contemplative sages; ਮਨਿ places their salutation inwardly.

jaap|jaap161.line02.simpleEn: You possess an enduring abundance of virtues.
jaap|jaap161.line02.simplePa: ਤੇਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਦਾ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਦੀ ਭਰਪੂਰਤਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap161.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਗੁਨਿ ਗਨ gathers the virtues together, while ਮੁਦਾਮ carries the sense of always.

jaap|jaap161.line03.simpleEn: Even the strongest adversaries cannot overcome You.
jaap|jaap161.line03.simplePa: ਵੱਡੇ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡੇ ਵੈਰੀ ਵੀ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਜਿੱਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਕਦੇ।
jaap|jaap161.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਰਿ ਬਰ names powerful adversaries; ਅਗੰਜ denies their power to defeat the Divine.

jaap|jaap161.line04.simpleEn: Sovereign of humankind, You also bring all to dissolution.
jaap|jaap161.line04.simplePa: ਮਨੁੱਖਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਾਲਕ, ਸਭ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਵੀ ਤੇਰੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap161.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਹਰਿ ਨਰ is read here as lordship over people, and ਪ੍ਰਭੰਜ retains the power of dissolution; the line does not simply repeat the preceding salutation.

jaap|jaap162.line01.simplePa: ਅਣਗਿਣਤ ਜੀਵ ਤੇਰੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਸਿਰ ਨਿਵਾਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ।
jaap|jaap162.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਗਨ expands the field of reverence beyond the sages named in the next line.

jaap|jaap162.line02.simpleEn: Sages salute You in their hearts.
jaap|jaap162.line02.simplePa: ਰਿਸ਼ੀ ਆਪਣੇ ਹਿਰਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੇਰੀ ਬੰਦਗੀ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਨ।
jaap|jaap162.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਸਲਾਮ and ਪ੍ਰਨਾਮ are two expressions of reverence within the same stanza.

jaap|jaap162.line03.simpleEn: You, sovereign of people, are whole and undivided.
jaap|jaap162.line03.simplePa: ਮਨੁੱਖਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਾਲਕ, ਤੂੰ ਸੰਪੂਰਨ ਅਤੇ ਅਖੰਡ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap162.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਖੰਡ expresses wholeness; the compound ਹਰਿ ਨਰ is read as Divine lordship, not a claim about a mortal ruler.

jaap|jaap162.line04.simpleEn: Supreme beyond humanity, You need no adornment.
jaap|jaap162.line04.simplePa: ਮਨੁੱਖਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਸਜਾਵਟ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap162.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਬਰ ਨਰ marks surpassing excellence; ਅਮੰਡ is taken here in its unadorned sense, not as an incomplete being.

jaap|jaap163.line01.simpleEn: Your knowing is self-arising, and You do not perish.
jaap|jaap163.line01.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਗਿਆਨ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਤੋਂ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਸ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦਾ।
jaap|jaap163.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਭਵ is read as knowledge not dependent on instruction from another; ਅਨਾਸ denies destruction.

jaap|jaap163.line02.simpleEn: You illumine the minds of the sages.
jaap|jaap163.line02.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਰਿਸ਼ੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਮਨਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਚਾਨਣ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap163.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ names illumination within the mind, continuing the contemplative language of the preceding stanzas.

jaap|jaap163.line03.simpleEn: To You, fullness of virtues, I bow.
jaap|jaap163.line03.simplePa: ਸਾਰੇ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਭਰਪੂਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਮੈਂ ਤੇਰੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਨਿਵਦਾ ਹਾਂ।
jaap|jaap163.line03.interpretiveCaution: The praise is addressed to the One described by ਗੁਨਿ ਗਨ; it need not be recast as a claim that virtues are separate worshippers.

jaap|jaap163.line04.simpleEn: You are always present in water and on land.
jaap|jaap163.line04.simplePa: ਜਲ ਅਤੇ ਧਰਤੀ ਉੱਤੇ ਤੂੰ ਹਰ ਵੇਲੇ ਹਾਜ਼ਰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap163.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਜਲ ਥਲ spans the lived world; ਮੁਦਾਮ adds enduring presence.

jaap|jaap164.line01.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਕਦੇ ਘਿਸਦਾ ਜਾਂ ਘਟਦਾ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap164.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅੰਗ is being or form in this praise; ਅਨਛਿੱਜ denies wearing out.

jaap|jaap164.line02.simpleEn: Your seat and abiding presence cannot be broken.
jaap|jaap164.line02.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੇਰਾ ਆਸਣ ਅਤੇ ਸਦਾ ਕਾਇਮ ਰਹਿਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਹਾਜ਼ਰੀ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap164.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਆਸਨ supplies an image of a seat or abiding place; ਅਭੰਗ denies its breaking.

jaap|jaap164.line03.simpleEn: Your likeness is beyond every comparison.
jaap|jaap164.line03.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਬਰਾਬਰੀ ਦਾ ਅੰਦਾਜ਼ਾ ਕਿਸੇ ਤੁਲਨਾ ਨਾਲ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਪੈਂਦਾ।
jaap|jaap164.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਉਪਮਾ concerns likeness or comparison, while ਅਪਾਰ marks what exceeds its limit.

jaap|jaap164.line04.simpleEn: Your state and measure surpass our reach.
jaap|jaap164.line04.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਅਵਸਥਾ ਅਤੇ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਦਾ ਮਾਪ ਸਾਡੀ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਡਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap164.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਗਤਿ and ਮਿਤਿ concern condition and extent; ਉਦਾਰ here carries vastness, not merely charitable giving.

jaap|jaap165.line01.simpleEn: Present in water and on land, You need no adornment.
jaap|jaap165.line01.simplePa: ਜਲ ਥਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਾਜ਼ਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਸਜਾਵਟ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap165.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਮੰਡ repeats the unadorned sense encountered in Chhand162.

jaap|jaap165.line02.simpleEn: In every direction, You are not born of Vishnu.
jaap|jaap165.line02.simplePa: ਹਰ ਦਿਸ਼ਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਤੂੰ ਵਿਸ਼ਨੂ ਤੋਂ ਪੈਦਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋਇਆ।
jaap|jaap165.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੰਡ is difficult. This note follows Sahib Singh's particular reading of independence from Vishnu; other explanations emphasize indivisibility. The source word is retained.

jaap|jaap165.line03.simpleEn: Throughout water and land, Your greatness prevails.
jaap|jaap165.line03.simplePa: ਜਲ ਅਤੇ ਧਰਤੀ ਭਰ ਤੇਰੀ ਮਹਾਨਤਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap165.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਮਹੰਤ expresses greatness here; it is not the title of a human religious office.

jaap|jaap165.line04.simpleEn: In every direction and every quarter, You are without limit.
jaap|jaap165.line04.simplePa: ਹਰ ਦਿਸ਼ਾ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਨੁੱਕਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੂੰ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap165.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਦਿਸ ਵਿਸ embraces directions and their intermediate quarters; ਬਿਅੰਤ refuses an outer boundary.

jaap|jaap166.line01.simpleEn: Your knowing is self-arising, and You do not perish.
jaap|jaap166.line01.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਗਿਆਨ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਤੋਂ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਸ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦਾ।
jaap|jaap166.line01.interpretiveCaution: This is an exact source-text repetition of Chhand163's opening; its meaning is retained while the surrounding images change.

jaap|jaap166.line02.simpleEn: You sustain the earth as its foremost sovereign.
jaap|jaap166.line02.simplePa: ਧਰਤੀ ਦਾ ਮੁੱਖ ਆਸਰਾ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਲਕ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap166.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਧ੍ਰਿਤ concerns the earth; ਧਰ ਧੁਰਾਸ expresses foremost lordship in the selected analysis.

jaap|jaap166.line03.simpleEn: The powers of creation lie within Your command.
jaap|jaap166.line03.simplePa: ਜਗਤ ਨੂੰ ਪੈਦਾ ਕਰਨ ਦੀਆਂ ਸ਼ਕਤੀਆਂ ਤੇਰੇ ਵੱਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਹਨ।
jaap|jaap166.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਆਜਾਨ ਬਾਹੁ is read with Sahib Singh as creative power under Divine command. A long-armed image is another traditional analysis; no source letters are altered.

jaap|jaap166.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਏਕੈ and ਸਦਾਹੁ bring the expanding descriptions back to enduring oneness.

jaap|jaap167.line01.simpleEn: Oankar, You are the primal source.
jaap|jaap167.line01.simplePa: ਹੇ ਓਅੰਕਾਰ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਦਾ ਮੂਲ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap167.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਓਅੰਕਾਰ names the Divine; ਆਦਿ relates the One to the world's origin.

jaap|jaap167.line02.simpleEn: No telling can reach a beginning of Yours.
jaap|jaap167.line02.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਵਰਣਨ ਤੇਰਾ ਮੁੱਢ ਨਹੀਂ ਲੱਭ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap167.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਕਥਨੀ and ਅਨਾਦਿ bring the attempt to describe the Divine beside its beginninglessness.

jaap|jaap167.line03.simpleEn: By Your very intent, the wicked are brought down.
jaap|jaap167.line03.simplePa: ਤੇਰੇ ਇੱਕ ਫੁਰਨੇ ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਦੁਸ਼ਟਾਂ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਹੋ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap167.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਖਲ names the wicked, ਖੰਡ breaking or destruction, and ਖਿਆਲ thought or intent.

jaap|jaap167.line04.simpleEn: You are supremely great and beyond death.
jaap|jaap167.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਮਹਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਮੌਤ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap167.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਗੁਰ ਬਰ is taken as surpassing greatness; ਅਕਾਲ expresses freedom from time and death.

jaap|jaap168.line01.simpleEn: In every home, reverence is offered to You.
jaap|jaap168.line01.simplePa: ਘਰ-ਘਰ ਤੇਰੇ ਅੱਗੇ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap168.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਘਰ ਘਰਿ widens the poetic field of devotion to inhabited life.

jaap|jaap168.line02.simpleEn: Your feet and Your Naam are cherished in the heart.
jaap|jaap168.line02.simplePa: ਹਿਰਦੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੇਰੇ ਚਰਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap168.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਚਰਨ carries devotional surrender and refuge; ਚਿਤ locates this remembrance inwardly.

jaap|jaap168.line03.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਕਦੇ ਪੁਰਾਣੀ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਮੁੱਕਦੀ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap168.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਗਾਤ is being or form, and ਅਨਛਿੱਜ recalls Chhand164's refusal of wearing away.

jaap|jaap168.line04.simpleEn: In nothing are You dependent or helpless.
jaap|jaap168.line04.simplePa: ਕਿਸੇ ਗੱਲ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਤੂੰ ਮੁਹਤਾਜ ਜਾਂ ਲਾਚਾਰ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap168.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਆਜਿਜ is read as helpless or dependent; ਨ ਬਾਤ extends the denial to every respect.

jaap|jaap169.line01.simpleEn: Your being is free from entangling strife.
jaap|jaap169.line01.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਝਗੜੇ ਅਤੇ ਉਲਝਣ ਦੀ ਪਕੜ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap169.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਝੰਝ denies entanglement in contention; ਗਾਤ again concerns being or form.

jaap|jaap169.line02.simpleEn: No matter brings resentment into You.
jaap|jaap169.line02.simplePa: ਕਿਸੇ ਗੱਲ ਨਾਲ ਤੇਰੇ ਵਿੱਚ ਰੰਜ ਨਹੀਂ ਪੈਦਾ ਹੁੰਦਾ।
jaap|jaap169.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਰੰਜ is read through freedom from rancour; ਬਾਤ is a matter or utterance, not a separate person.

jaap|jaap169.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਟੁਟ and ਭੰਡਾਰ present inexhaustible abundance.

jaap|jaap169.line04.simpleEn: You cannot be set up or confined; You are without limit.
jaap|jaap169.line04.simplePa: ਤੈਨੂੰ ਬਣਾਕੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਹੱਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਟਿਕਾਇਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ; ਤੂੰ ਬੇਅੰਤ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap169.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਠਟ is read as not established by another; ਅਪਾਰ reinforces unboundedness.

jaap|jaap170.line01.simpleEn: Your sustaining order exceeds what we can see.
jaap|jaap170.line01.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਧਰਮ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਭਾਉਣ ਦਾ ਢੰਗ ਸਾਡੀ ਵੇਖੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap170.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਆਡੀਠ concerns the unseen or unparalleled; ਧਰਮ is read here as sustaining duty or order, not a label for one religious community.

jaap|jaap170.line02.simpleEn: Your actions are steadfast and fearless.
jaap|jaap170.line02.simplePa: ਤੇਰੇ ਕਰਮ ਦ੍ਰਿੜ੍ਹ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਡਰ ਹਨ।
jaap|jaap170.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਢੀਠ here praises resolute action; it should not be reduced to the everyday pejorative stubborn.

jaap|jaap170.line03.simpleEn: You cannot be wounded, and You are without end.
jaap|jaap170.line03.simplePa: ਤੈਨੂੰ ਜ਼ਖ਼ਮੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਰਾ ਅੰਤ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap170.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਣਬ੍ਰਣ denies a wound; ਅਨੰਤ adds limitlessness.

jaap|jaap170.line04.simpleEn: You are the supremely great Giver.
jaap|jaap170.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਮਹਾਨ ਦਾਤਾਰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap170.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਦਾਤਾ closes this Madhubhar sequence with generosity, alongside the preceding power and endurance.

jaap|jaap171.line01.simpleEn: You are the dwelling of compassion.
jaap|jaap171.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਕਰੁਣਾ and ਆਲਯ combine compassion with the image of a dwelling or abode.

jaap|jaap171.line02.simpleEn: You bring adversaries to their end.
jaap|jaap171.line02.simplePa: ਵੈਰੀਆਂ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap171.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਰਿ ਘਾਲਯ retains the force of overcoming adversaries; it is more than a general statement about comfort.

jaap|jaap171.line03.simplePa: ਦੁਸ਼ਟਾਂ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap171.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਖਲ means the wicked, while ਖੰਡਨ conveys breaking or destroying.

jaap|jaap171.line04.simplePa: ਧਰਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਬਣਾਉਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap171.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਮਹਿ names the earth; ਮੰਡਨ names adornment or beautifying.

jaap|jaap172.line01.simpleEn: You are the sovereign of the world.
jaap|jaap172.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਜਗਤੇਸ੍ਵਰ joins the world with lordship; it addresses the Divine rather than a worldly ruler.

jaap|jaap172.line02.simplePa: ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚਾ ਮਾਲਕ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap172.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਪਰਮੇਸ੍ਵਰ heightens the preceding address through supreme lordship.

jaap|jaap172.line03.simpleEn: You are the source even of strife.
jaap|jaap172.line03.simplePa: ਕਲਹ ਦਾ ਕਾਰਣ ਵੀ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap172.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਕਲਿ is retained exactly. The main reading follows strife or suffering; an age-of-Kali reading also occurs. It is not silently changed to ਕਲਾ.

jaap|jaap172.line04.simpleEn: You are the deliverer of all.
jaap|jaap172.line04.simplePa: ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਉਬਾਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap172.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਉਬਾਰਣ gives the stanza its movement toward rescue or deliverance.

jaap|jaap173.line01.simpleEn: You are the support of the earth.
jaap|jaap173.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਧ੍ਰਿਤ ਕੇ ਧ੍ਰਣ relates the earth to that which sustains it.

jaap|jaap173.line02.simpleEn: You are the cause of the world.
jaap|jaap173.line02.simplePa: ਜਗਤ ਦੇ ਬਣਨ ਦਾ ਕਾਰਣ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap173.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਕ੍ਰਣ is read as cause or making; the source's contracted spelling is preserved.

jaap|jaap173.line03.simpleEn: You are worthy of the heart's trust.
jaap|jaap173.line03.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੰਨਣ ਅਤੇ ਭਰੋਸਾ ਕਰਨ ਜੋਗ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap173.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਮਨ ਮਾਨਿਯ moves from cosmic support to inward acknowledgment.

jaap|jaap173.line04.simpleEn: You are the One acknowledged throughout the world.
jaap|jaap173.line04.simplePa: ਜਗਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਹੀ ਪਛਾਣਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਮੰਨਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap173.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਜਗ ਜਾਨਿਯ is expansive praise of the One known or worthy of being known in the world.

jaap|jaap174.line01.simplePa: ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਲਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap174.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਭਰ gives the sense of sustaining or nourishing, with ਸਰਬੰ extending it to all.

jaap|jaap174.line02.simplePa: ਸਭ ਨੂੰ ਪੈਦਾ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap174.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਕਰ is the making or creating term within this repeated universal frame.

jaap|jaap174.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਪਾਸਿਯ is read through nearness, not as a reference to a particular spatial side.

jaap|jaap174.line04.simpleEn: You bring all to their end.
jaap|jaap174.line04.simplePa: ਸਭ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਵੀ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap174.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਨਾਸਿਯ retains dissolution as the final member of the stanza, alongside support, creation and nearness.

jaap|jaap175.line01.simpleEn: You are the source of compassion.
jaap|jaap175.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਕਰੁਣਾਕਰ brings compassion together with the sense of a source or treasury.

jaap|jaap175.line02.simplePa: ਸਾਰੇ ਜਗਤ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਲਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap175.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਬਿਸ੍ਵੰਭਰ joins the world with sustaining or nourishing.

jaap|jaap175.line03.simpleEn: You are the sovereign of all.
jaap|jaap175.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਸਰਬੇਸ੍ਵਰ names lordship without restricting its scope to one group.

jaap|jaap175.line04.simpleEn: You are the sovereign of the world.
jaap|jaap175.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਜਗਤੇਸ੍ਵਰ returns the stanza to the world's shared Divine source.

jaap|jaap176.line01.simpleEn: You are the sovereign of the cosmos.
jaap|jaap176.line01.simplePa: ਸਾਰੇ ਬ੍ਰਹਿਮੰਡ ਦਾ ਮਾਲਕ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap176.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਬ੍ਰਹਮੰਡਸ is read as lordship over the cosmic whole.

jaap|jaap176.line02.simplePa: ਦੁਸ਼ਟਾਂ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap176.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਖਲ ਖੰਡਸ repeats the moral force of breaking wickedness in a compact compound.

jaap|jaap176.line03.simpleEn: You are beyond even the highest.
jaap|jaap176.line03.simplePa: ਉੱਚੇ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚੇ ਤੋਂ ਵੀ ਪਰੇ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap176.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਪਰ ਤੇ ਪਰ moves beyond any final rank or comparison the mind proposes.

jaap|jaap176.line04.simpleEn: You are the source of compassion.
jaap|jaap176.line04.interpretiveCaution: The closing ਕਰੁਣਾਕਰ brings the transcendent praise back to compassion.

jaap|jaap177.line01.simpleEn: You are the One remembered, beyond being captured by recitation.
jaap|jaap177.line01.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਜਪਣ ਜੋਗ ਹੈਂ, ਪਰ ਜਪ ਦੀ ਪਕੜ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੱਝਦਾ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap177.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜਪਾ ਜਪ joins remembrance to what cannot be confined or controlled by a formula; the phrase is also associated with unspoken remembrance.

jaap|jaap177.line02.simpleEn: No one can install or establish You.
jaap|jaap177.line02.simplePa: ਤੈਨੂੰ ਕੋਈ ਥਾਪ ਕੇ ਸਥਾਪਿਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap177.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਥਪਾ ਥਪ denies dependence upon another's act of installation.

jaap|jaap177.line03.simpleEn: No fashioned image can contain Your being.
jaap|jaap177.line03.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਘੜਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਰੂਪ ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮੇਟ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap177.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਕ੍ਰਿਤਾ ਕ੍ਰਿਤ is read with the beyond-a-fashioned-image interpretation; an uncreated-Creator analysis also appears in commentary.

jaap|jaap177.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਅਮਰ ਹੈਂ, ਮੌਤ ਦੀ ਪਕੜ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ।
jaap|jaap177.line04.interpretiveCaution: The selected direct-source reading is ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਾ ਮ੍ਰਿਤ, with tippi. Other witnesses omit it or join the compound. The meaning follows the deathlessness sense without harmonizing the source text.

jaap|jaap178.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਮ੍ਰਿਤਾ ਮ੍ਰਿਤ is read as a compact deathlessness expression. Its spelling is retained separately from the tippi reading at177.

jaap|jaap178.line02.simpleEn: Compassion takes expression in Your being.
jaap|jaap178.line02.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਇਆ ਦਾ ਪ੍ਰਗਟਾਵਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap178.line02.interpretiveCaution: The selected source writes ਕਰਣਾ ਕ੍ਰਿਤ. The compassion reading follows commentary on the corresponding ਕਰੁਣਾ compound in other witnesses; the variant is disclosed, not silently rewritten.

jaap|jaap178.line03.simpleEn: No fashioned image can contain Your being.
jaap|jaap178.line03.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਘੜਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਰੂਪ ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮੇਟ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap178.line03.interpretiveCaution: This exact ਅਕ੍ਰਿਤਾ ਕ੍ਰਿਤ source string also occurs at177 and179; its main wording is retained.

jaap|jaap178.line04.simpleEn: You are the support of the earth.
jaap|jaap178.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਧਰਣੀ names the earth and ਧ੍ਰਿਤ its sustaining support.

jaap|jaap179.line01.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਮਾਪ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਮਾਲਕ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap179.line01.interpretiveCaution: The selected ਅਮਿਤੇਸ੍ਵਰ is read from ਅਮਿਤ, immeasurable. A different ਅਮ੍ਰਿਤੇਸ੍ਵਰ reading supports a nectar-related gloss; that is not substituted here.

jaap|jaap179.line02.simplePa: ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚਾ ਮਾਲਕ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap179.line02.interpretiveCaution: This exact source phrase also occurs at172; its main meaning remains consistent.

jaap|jaap179.line03.simpleEn: No fashioned image can contain Your being.
jaap|jaap179.line03.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਘੜਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਰੂਪ ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮੇਟ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap179.line03.interpretiveCaution: The same exact phrase at177 and178 is retained, now framed by immeasurability and supremacy.

jaap|jaap179.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਸਦਾ ਮੌਤ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap179.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਮ੍ਰਿਤਾ ਮ੍ਰਿਤ continues the repeated deathlessness praise; the terminal source spacing and counter remain unchanged.

jaap|jaap180.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜਬਾ ਕ੍ਰਿਤ is read through wondrous form or manifestation, rather than an ordinary made object.

jaap|jaap180.line02.simpleEn: You are the deathless essence of life-giving nectar.
jaap|jaap180.line02.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਅਮਰ ਹੈਂ, ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਅਮਰ ਰਸ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap180.line02.interpretiveCaution: The selected ਅਮ੍ਰਿਤਾ ਅਮ੍ਰਿਤ repeats the amrit term. It permits the nectar image alongside deathlessness; other witnesses vary this compound.

jaap|jaap180.line03.simpleEn: You are the guide and sovereign of humankind.
jaap|jaap180.line03.simplePa: ਮਨੁੱਖਾਂ ਦਾ ਆਗੂ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਲਕ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap180.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਨਰ ਨਾਇਕ places human life under Divine guidance.

jaap|jaap180.line04.simplePa: ਦੁਸ਼ਟਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਨਾਸ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap180.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਖਲ ਘਾਇਕ keeps the force of striking or defeating wickedness.

jaap|jaap181.line01.simplePa: ਸਾਰੇ ਜਗਤ ਨੂੰ ਪਾਲਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap181.line01.interpretiveCaution: This exact ਬਿਸ੍ਵੰਭਰ phrase appeared at175; its world-sustaining meaning is retained.

jaap|jaap181.line02.simpleEn: You are the dwelling of compassion.
jaap|jaap181.line02.interpretiveCaution: The exact ਕਰੁਣਾਲਯ phrase returns from171, now beside nourishment and protection.

jaap|jaap181.line03.simpleEn: You are the sovereign over rulers.
jaap|jaap181.line03.simplePa: ਰਾਜਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਵੀ ਮਾਲਕ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap181.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਨ੍ਰਿਪ names rulers; ਨਾਇਕ places their power under a greater sovereignty.

jaap|jaap181.line04.simpleEn: You are the protector of all.
jaap|jaap181.line04.simplePa: ਸਭ ਦੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap181.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਪਾਇਕ is read as protecting in this context, alongside the universal ਸਰਬ.

jaap|jaap182.line01.simpleEn: You free beings from the round of birth and death.
jaap|jaap182.line01.simplePa: ਜਨਮ ਮਰਨ ਦੇ ਗੇੜ ਤੋਂ ਛੁਡਾਉਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap182.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਭਵ ਭੰਜਨ retains the religious horizon of worldly becoming and release, not only everyday worry.

jaap|jaap182.line02.simplePa: ਵੈਰੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਜਿੱਤਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap182.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਰਿ ਗੰਜਨ is the overcoming of adversarial power.

jaap|jaap182.line03.simplePa: ਵੈਰੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਤਪਾਉਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap182.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਰਿਪੁ ਤਾਪਨ retains the stronger image of causing adversaries distress; it is not softened into a generic comfort phrase.

jaap|jaap182.line04.simpleEn: You inspire the remembrance by which You are remembered.
jaap|jaap182.line04.simplePa: ਆਪਣਾ ਜਾਪ ਜਪਾਉਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਵੀ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap182.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਜਾਪਨ is read causatively: the Divine enables the act of remembrance itself.

jaap|jaap183.line01.simpleEn: Your being is free from stain.
jaap|jaap183.line01.simplePa: ਤੇਰੇ ਸਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੋਈ ਦਾਗ਼ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap183.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਕਲੰ ਕ੍ਰਿਤ is read as the unstained-form compound, not as a claim that the Divine lacks intelligence.

jaap|jaap183.line02.simpleEn: Your being is complete and perfect.
jaap|jaap183.line02.interpretiveCaution: The main reading takes ਸਰਬ as complete, following Sahib Singh. An all-form explanation is also encountered; it is not substituted for the chosen complete-being analysis.

jaap|jaap183.line03.simpleEn: You are the maker even of creators.
jaap|jaap183.line03.simplePa: ਰਚਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਪੈਦਾ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap183.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਕਰਤਾ ਕਰ places any subordinate creative power within Divine origination.

jaap|jaap183.line04.simpleEn: You bring even destroyers to their end.
jaap|jaap183.line04.simplePa: ਨਾਸ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਵੀ ਤੇਰੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap183.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਹਰਤਾ ਹਰਿ intensifies the dissolution language through the destroyer of destroyers.

jaap|jaap184.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਪਰਮਾਤਮ names the supreme Divine reality through the vocabulary of self or soul.

jaap|jaap184.line02.simpleEn: You are the Self present in all.
jaap|jaap184.line02.simplePa: ਸਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਤਮ-ਰੂਪ ਤੂੰ ਹੀ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap184.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਸਰਬਾਤਮ joins all with self, retaining universal indwelling rather than restricting the line to the origin of separate souls.

jaap|jaap184.line03.simpleEn: You are governed by Yourself alone.
jaap|jaap184.line03.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਦੇ ਹੀ ਵੱਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap184.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਆਤਮ ਬਸ expresses self-dependence and freedom from another's command.

jaap|jaap184.line04.simpleEn: You remain just as You are.
jaap|jaap184.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਜਿਹੋ ਜਿਹਾ ਹੈਂ, ਸਦਾ ਉਹੋ ਜਿਹਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap184.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਜਸ ਕੇ ਜਸ is read as remaining as oneself, following Sahib Singh's explanation; it is not read here as glory of glories.

jaap|jaap185.line01.simpleEn: Salutations to You, the sun of suns and the moon of moons.
jaap|jaap185.line01.simplePa: ਸੂਰਜਾਂ ਦੇ ਸੂਰਜ ਅਤੇ ਚੰਦਰਮਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਚੰਦਰਮਾ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap185.line01.interpretiveCaution: The doubled images praise the source of radiance through sun and moon; both images should remain visible.

jaap|jaap185.line02.simpleEn: Salutations to You, sovereign of sovereigns and lord even of Indra.
jaap|jaap185.line02.simplePa: ਰਾਜਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਰਾਜੇ ਅਤੇ ਇੰਦਰ ਦੇ ਵੀ ਮਾਲਕ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap185.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਇੰਦ੍ਰ is retained as the traditional sovereign-of-the-gods image rather than silently replaced with a modern ruler.

jaap|jaap185.line03.simpleEn: Salutations to You as darkness, and as radiance beyond radiance.
jaap|jaap185.line03.simplePa: ਹਨੇਰੇ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਜਾਂ ਦੇ ਤੇਜ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap185.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅੰਧਕਾਰੇ and ਤੇਜ are deliberately held together. The source does not say only destroyer of darkness here.

jaap|jaap185.line04.simpleEn: Salutations to You, gathering of all gatherings and source within every seed.
jaap|jaap185.line04.simplePa: ਸਮੂਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਮੂਹ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਬੀਜ ਦੇ ਮੂਲ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap185.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਬ੍ਰਿੰਦ gathers the many; ਬੀਜ turns toward origin and the subtle source of life.

jaap|jaap186.line01.simpleEn: Salutations to You in the forms of activity, darkness and serenity.
jaap|jaap186.line01.simplePa: ਰਜਸ, ਤਮਸ ਅਤੇ ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਦੇ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap186.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਰਾਜਸੰ, ਤਾਮਸੰ and ਸਾਂਤ name the traditional qualities of active desire, inertia or darkness, and peaceful balance.

jaap|jaap186.line02.simpleEn: Salutations to the supreme reality, whose being exceeds created elements.
jaap|jaap186.line02.simplePa: ਪਰਮ ਹਕੀਕਤ ਅਤੇ ਜਗਤ ਦੇ ਤੱਤਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਸਰੂਪ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap186.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਪਰਮ ਤੱਤੰ and ਅਤੱਤੰ place supreme reality beside freedom from the constituents of creation; the chosen explanation follows the preceding qualities context.

jaap|jaap186.line03.simpleEn: Salutations to the supreme spiritual union and the highest knowing.
jaap|jaap186.line03.simplePa: ਜੋਗਾਂ ਦੇ ਜੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਗਿਆਨਾਂ ਦੇ ਗਿਆਨ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap186.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਜੋਗ and ਗਿਆਨ retain their distinct senses of spiritual discipline or union and knowledge.

jaap|jaap186.line04.simpleEn: Salutations to You, mantra of mantras and depth of meditation.
jaap|jaap186.line04.simplePa: ਮੰਤਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਮੰਤਰ ਅਤੇ ਧਿਆਨ ਦੀ ਗਹਿਰਾਈ, ਤੈਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap186.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਮੰਤ੍ਰ and ਧਿਆਨ remain distinct practices or forms of attention, both centred on the Divine.

jaap|jaap187.line01.simpleEn: Salutations to the victor in battle and to knowledge beyond knowledge.
jaap|jaap187.line01.simplePa: ਜੁੱਧ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਿੱਤਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਅਤੇ ਗਿਆਨਾਂ ਦੇ ਗਿਆਨ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap187.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਜੁਧ ਜੁਧੇ is read through victory in struggle; ਗਿਆਨ ਗਿਆਨੇ keeps knowing beside the martial image.

jaap|jaap187.line02.simpleEn: Salutations to the sustainer through food and the provider of drink.
jaap|jaap187.line02.simplePa: ਭੋਜਨ ਨਾਲ ਪਾਲਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਅਤੇ ਪਾਨ ਦੇ ਆਸਰੇ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap187.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਭੋਜ and ਪਾਨ are read here as nourishment and drink. Sahib Singh instead explains ਪਾਨ through hand, with creatures’ food in Divine hands; this alternate analysis is retained explicitly.

jaap|jaap187.line03.simpleEn: Salutations to the source of conflict and the embodiment of peace.
jaap|jaap187.line03.simplePa: ਕਲਹ ਦੇ ਕਰਤੇ ਅਤੇ ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਦੇ ਸਰੂਪ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap187.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਕਲਹ ਕਰਤਾ and ਸਾਂਤ ਰੂਪੇ are both retained; the source holds conflict and peace in the same address.

jaap|jaap187.line04.simpleEn: Salutations to the lord even of Indra, whose splendour has no beginning.
jaap|jaap187.line04.simplePa: ਇੰਦਰ ਦੇ ਵੀ ਮਾਲਕ ਅਤੇ ਮੁੱਢ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਤਾਪ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap187.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਾਦੰ qualifies splendour as beginningless; the Indra image belongs to the traditional field of sovereignty.

jaap|jaap188.line01.simpleEn: Your being opposes every stain; You are the adornment of adornments.
jaap|jaap188.line01.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਦਾਗ਼ ਦਾ ਵਿਰੋਧੀ ਹੈ; ਸਾਰੀਆਂ ਸਜਾਵਟਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੋਭਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap188.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਕਲੰਕਾਰ is read in the unstained or enemy-of-stain sense, as in Sahib Singh's ਕਲੰਕਾਰਿ discussion. The selected source spelling is retained.

jaap|jaap188.line02.simpleEn: Salutations to the support of every hope, the beauty of all beauty.
jaap|jaap188.line02.simplePa: ਸਭ ਆਸਾਂ ਦੇ ਆਸਰੇ ਅਤੇ ਸੁੰਦਰਾਂ ਦੇ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ।
jaap|jaap188.line02.interpretiveCaution: The selected ਬਾਂਕ supports the beautiful or graceful sense. A ਬਾਕ reading in another witness leads to a speech-related interpretation.

jaap|jaap188.line03.simpleEn: Your being is unbroken, bodiless and beyond any single defining name.
jaap|jaap188.line03.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਹੈ, ਸਰੀਰ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੱਝਦੀ।
jaap|jaap188.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੰਗੀ, ਅਨੰਗੀ and ਅਨਾਮੇ are distinct descriptions: undestroyed, without bodily limitation, and not confined by a name.

jaap|jaap188.line04.simpleEn: You dissolve the three worlds and abide through all three times, bodiless and free of desire.
jaap|jaap188.line04.simplePa: ਤਿੰਨਾਂ ਭਵਨਾਂ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਵੀ ਤੇਰੇ ਵੱਸ ਹੈ; ਤੂੰ ਤਿੰਨਾਂ ਕਾਲਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਹੈਂ, ਅੰਗਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਕਾਮਨਾ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ।
jaap|jaap188.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਤ੍ਰਿਭੰਗੀ is read as dissolving the three worlds and ਤ੍ਰਿਕਾਲੇ as past, present and future; this follows the selected commentarial analysis rather than a physical three-bent pose.

jaap|jaap189.line01.simplePa: ਤੈਨੂੰ ਕਦੇ ਜਿੱਤਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap189.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜੈ is a compact praise of invincibility.

jaap|jaap189.line02.simpleEn: You do not dissolve or perish.
jaap|jaap189.line02.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਲੈਅ ਜਾਂ ਨਾਸ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੁੰਦਾ।
jaap|jaap189.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਲੈ denies dissolution; it is not a command to avoid change in ordinary life.

jaap|jaap189.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੈ names fearlessness in the Divine addressee.

jaap|jaap189.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਬੈ is read as freedom from death, completing the stanza's cluster of invincibility and endurance.

jaap|jaap190.line01.simpleEn: You do not come into birth.
jaap|jaap190.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੂ denies arising into birth or created existence.

jaap|jaap190.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜੂ is read in the unmoving sense explained by Sahib Singh; it is not automatically collapsed into the preceding unborn term.

jaap|jaap190.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਾਸ denies destruction while retaining its own place beside birth and movement.

jaap|jaap190.line04.simplePa: ਆਕਾਸ਼ ਵਾਂਗ ਤੂੰ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap190.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਕਾਸ supplies the space or sky image for pervasiveness; it is not a claim that the Divine is identical with a measured physical sky.

jaap|jaap191.line01.simplePa: ਤੈਨੂੰ ਵੱਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਰਕੇ ਹਰਾਇਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap191.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਗੰਜ praises freedom from defeat or subjugation.

jaap|jaap191.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੰਜ concerns breaking or destroying, distinct from being defeated.

jaap|jaap191.line03.simpleEn: You are beyond the grasp of sight.
jaap|jaap191.line03.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਨਜ਼ਰ ਦੀ ਪਕੜ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap191.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਲੱਖ is the unseen or ungrasped; its addak is retained in the source.

jaap|jaap191.line04.simpleEn: You need no food to sustain You.
jaap|jaap191.line04.simplePa: ਤੈਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੀ ਹੋਂਦ ਲਈ ਕਿਸੇ ਖੁਰਾਕ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap191.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੱਖ is read as not requiring food, rather than a direction for human fasting.

jaap|jaap192.line01.simpleEn: You are beyond time and death.
jaap|jaap192.line01.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਕਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਮੌਤ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap192.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਕਾਲ carries the freedom from time's destructive limit.

jaap|jaap192.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਦਿਆਲ is a positive relational description among the surrounding negating epithets.

jaap|jaap192.line03.simpleEn: No written or pictured form can encompass You.
jaap|jaap192.line03.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਲਿਖਤ ਜਾਂ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਤੇਰਾ ਪੂਰਾ ਰੂਪ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮੇਟ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap192.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਲੇਖ is read through what cannot be fully inscribed or depicted.

jaap|jaap192.line04.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਬਾਹਰਲਾ ਭੇਖ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਕਰ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap192.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਭੇਖ denies a defining costume or guise; it does not identify a particular human garment as bad.

jaap|jaap193.line01.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਮ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਘੇਰ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap193.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਾਮ is read with the bani's many Divine names: no exclusive designation exhausts the One.

jaap|jaap193.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਅਕਾਮ denies self-seeking desire, alongside the compassion praised elsewhere.

jaap|jaap193.line03.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਗਹਿਰਾਈ ਦਾ ਪਾਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਪਾਇਆ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap193.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਗਾਹ uses the image of depth beyond sounding.

jaap|jaap193.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਢਾਹ concerns freedom from being overthrown or demolished.

jaap|jaap194.line01.simplePa: ਤੇਰੇ ਉੱਤੇ ਕੋਈ ਹੋਰ ਮਾਲਕ ਨਹੀਂ।
jaap|jaap194.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਨਾਥੇ is read as having no superior lord, not as helpless orphanhood.

jaap|jaap194.line02.simplePa: ਸਭ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap194.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਪ੍ਰਮਾਥੇ retains its force of bringing down or destroying.

jaap|jaap194.line03.simpleEn: You are beyond birth in any womb.
jaap|jaap194.line03.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਕਿਸੇ ਜੂਨ ਦੇ ਜਨਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਉਂਦਾ।
jaap|jaap194.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜੋਨੀ denies entering the cycle of embodied birth.

jaap|jaap194.line04.simpleEn: You are not confined to silence.
jaap|jaap194.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਮੋਨੀ is read with the silence-vow sense of ਮੋਨੀ. It is not a claim about how loudly a person should recite.

jaap|jaap195.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਰਾਗੇ is read as attachment in this sequence, not as a denial of the value of musical raag.

jaap|jaap195.line02.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਰੰਗ ਤੇਰੀ ਪੂਰੀ ਪਛਾਣ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਣਦਾ।
jaap|jaap195.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਰੰਗੇ denies confinement to a particular colour.

jaap|jaap195.line03.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਰੂਪ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਘੇਰਦਾ।
jaap|jaap195.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਰੂਪੇ is read with the following mark or outline term and the bani's wider language of unconfined being.

jaap|jaap195.line04.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਰੇਖ ਜਾਂ ਨਿਸ਼ਾਨ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮੇਟਦਾ।
jaap|jaap195.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਰੇਖੇ concerns a delineating mark or outline; its scope is description, not a direction to erase human differences.

jaap|jaap196.line01.simpleEn: You are free from dependence on ritual action.
jaap|jaap196.line01.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਕਰਮ-ਕਾਂਡ ਦੀ ਮੁਹਤਾਜੀ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap196.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਅਕਰਮੰ is read as freedom from the need or bond of prescribed actions, not as denying all Divine activity.

jaap|jaap196.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਗੰਜੇ returns to a recurring description of invincibility.

jaap|jaap196.line04.simpleEn: No description or depiction can contain You.
jaap|jaap196.line04.simplePa: ਕੋਈ ਵਰਣਨ ਜਾਂ ਚਿੱਤਰ ਤੈਨੂੰ ਪੂਰਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਸਮੇਟ ਸਕਦਾ।
jaap|jaap196.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅਲੇਖੇ closes this short-form section by marking the limit of inscribing or depicting the Divine.

jaap|jaap197.line01.simpleEn: I bow before the One worthy of reverence, who brings all to dissolution.
jaap|jaap197.line01.simplePa: ਬੰਦਗੀ ਜੋਗ ਅਤੇ ਸਭ ਦਾ ਅੰਤ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਅੱਗੇ ਮੈਂ ਨਿਵਦਾ ਹਾਂ।
jaap|jaap197.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਪ੍ਰਨਾਮੇ and ਪ੍ਰਣਾਸੇ sound close but carry different meanings: reverence and dissolution.

jaap|jaap197.line02.simpleEn: Unconquerable and beyond any single name, You dwell in all.
jaap|jaap197.line02.simplePa: ਅਜਿੱਤ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਮ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap197.line02.interpretiveCaution: The line places invincibility and unconfined naming beside universal indwelling.

jaap|jaap197.line03.simpleEn: Free of desire in Your splendour, You are present as every form.
jaap|jaap197.line03.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਪ੍ਰਤਾਪ ਕਾਮਨਾ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਰੂਪ ਤੇਰਾ ਹੀ ਸਰੂਪ ਹਨ।
jaap|jaap197.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਨ੍ਰਿਕਾਮੰ is retained as the source spelling for desirelessness; ਸਮਸਤੁਲ ਸਰੂਪੇ broadens the statement to all forms.

jaap|jaap197.line04.simpleEn: You destroy wrongful action; righteous duty displays Your splendour.
jaap|jaap197.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਮੰਦੇ ਕਰਮਾਂ ਦਾ ਨਾਸ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈਂ; ਨੇਕ ਧਰਮ ਵਿੱਚ ਤੇਰਾ ਪ੍ਰਤਾਪ ਦਿਸਦਾ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap197.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਕੁਕਰਮੰ and ਸੁਧਰਮੰ distinguish wrongdoing from righteous duty, making the stanza's ethical contrast explicit.

jaap|jaap198.line01.simpleEn: Ever truth, awareness and bliss, You destroy adversaries.
jaap|jaap198.line01.simplePa: ਸਦਾ ਸੱਚੀ ਹੋਂਦ, ਚੇਤਨਾ ਅਤੇ ਆਨੰਦ-ਰੂਪ ਤੂੰ ਵੈਰੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਨਾਸ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap198.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਸੱਚਿਦਾਨੰਦ holds being, consciousness and bliss together; ਸੱਤ੍ਰੰ ਪ੍ਰਣਾਸੀ retains the adversarial description beside it.

jaap|jaap198.line02.simpleEn: Gracious Creator, You dwell within all.
jaap|jaap198.line02.simplePa: ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਰਚਨਹਾਰ, ਤੂੰ ਸਭ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap198.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਕਰੀਮੁਲ, ਕੁਨਿੰਦਾ and ਨਿਵਾਸੀ gather generosity, creating and indwelling in one line.

jaap|jaap198.line03.simpleEn: Wondrous is Your splendour; You bring wrath upon adversaries.
jaap|jaap198.line03.simplePa: ਤੇਰਾ ਪ੍ਰਤਾਪ ਅਚਰਜ ਹੈ; ਤੂੰ ਵੈਰੀਆਂ ਉੱਤੇ ਕਹਿਰ ਲਿਆਉਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap198.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਅਜਾਇਬ names wonder; ਗਜਾਇਬ ਗਨੀਮੇ retains the fierce or wrathful relation to enemies rather than erasing it.

jaap|jaap198.line04.simpleEn: You take away and create, generous and merciful.
jaap|jaap198.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਹਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ ਅਤੇ ਰਚਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਹੈਂ, ਬਖ਼ਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਅਤੇ ਰਹਿਮ ਨਾਲ ਭਰਪੂਰ।
jaap|jaap198.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਹਰੀਅੰ and ਕਰੀਅੰ are read as taking away and creating, followed by ਕਰੀਮਲੁ and ਰਹੀਮੇ, generosity and mercy.

jaap|jaap199.line01.simpleEn: You pervade every quarter and hold sovereignty throughout them all.
jaap|jaap199.line01.simplePa: ਚਹੁੰ ਪਾਸੀਂ ਤੂੰ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਹੈਂ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਪਾਸੇ ਤੇਰੀ ਮਾਲਕੀ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap199.line01.interpretiveCaution: ਚੱਤ੍ਰ ਚੱਕ੍ਰ marks the four quarters as an image of everywhere. ਭੁਗਤੇ is read here as sovereign enjoyment or rule, not as a geographical restriction.

jaap|jaap199.line02.simpleEn: Self-existent and beautiful, You are always joined with all.
jaap|jaap199.line02.simplePa: ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਤੋਂ ਹੋਂਦ ਵਾਲੇ ਸੁੰਦਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ, ਤੂੰ ਸਦਾ ਸਭ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap199.line02.interpretiveCaution: ਸੁਯੰਭਵ concerns self-existence; ਸੁਭੰ beauty or auspiciousness; ਸਰਬ ਜੁਗਤੇ universal relation.

jaap|jaap199.line03.simpleEn: You end the anguish of birth and death, the very embodiment of compassion.
jaap|jaap199.line03.simplePa: ਜਨਮ ਮਰਨ ਦੀ ਔਖਿਆਈ ਮਿਟਾਉਣ ਵਾਲੇ, ਤੂੰ ਦਇਆ ਦਾ ਸਰੂਪ ਹੈਂ।
jaap|jaap199.line03.interpretiveCaution: ਦੁਕਾਲੰ is read with Sahib Singh as the two occasions of birth and death. A broader adversity or distress reading is also encountered; no source wording is changed.

jaap|jaap199.line04.simpleEn: You are always beside us, Your splendour unbroken.
jaap|jaap199.line04.simplePa: ਤੂੰ ਸਦਾ ਸਾਡੇ ਅੰਗ-ਸੰਗ ਹੈਂ; ਤੇਰਾ ਪ੍ਰਤਾਪ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਹੈ।
jaap|jaap199.line04.interpretiveCaution: ਅੰਗ ਸੰਗੇ closes on intimate companionship; ਅਭੰਗੰ ਬਿਭੂਤੇ retains enduring splendour. This is the final numbered stanza of the selected Jaap Sahib source.

anand|anand24.line01.simpleEn: Without the True Guru, other speech remains spiritually unripe.
anand|anand24.line01.simplePa: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਤੋਂ ਬਿਨਾ ਹੋਰ ਬਾਣੀ ਆਤਮਕ ਪੱਖੋਂ ਕੱਚੀ ਹੈ।
anand|anand24.line01.interpretiveCaution: Kachi literally evokes what is unripe or not firm. The spiritual qualification is an explanatory choice; the source expressly names the True Guru.

anand|anand24.line02.simpleEn: Such speech is unripe: apart from the True Guru, other speech remains unripe.
anand|anand24.line02.simplePa: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਦੇ ਆਸਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਬਿਨਾ ਹੋਰ ਬਾਣੀ ਕੱਚੀ ਹੀ ਰਹਿੰਦੀ ਹੈ।
anand|anand24.line02.interpretiveCaution: The repeated wording emphasizes the same criterion. It should be read with Pauri 23, which invites the Guru’s beloved Sikhs to sing true Bani.

anand|anand24.line03.simpleEn: Unsteady are those who speak it and those who hear it; it is expounded by the spiritually unsteady.
anand|anand24.line03.simplePa: ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਆਖਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਣਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਆਤਮਕ ਤੌਰ ਉੱਤੇ ਕੱਚੇ ਹਨ; ਕੱਚੇ ਮਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਹੀ ਇਸ ਨੂੰ ਆਖ ਕੇ ਸਮਝਾਉਂਦੇ ਹਨ।
anand|anand24.line03.interpretiveCaution: The final kachin is read as an agentive plural: by the unripe or unsteady. This follows the contextual grammatical reading in Sahib Singh’s Darpan. The original text uses the exact normal-Unicode sequence of the selected source edition.

anand|anand24.line04.simpleEn: Their tongues keep saying “Hari, Hari,” yet they do not understand what they say.
anand|anand24.line04.simplePa: ਜੀਭ ਨਾਲ ਨਿੱਤ ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ, ਪਰ ਆਪਣੇ ਕਹੇ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਨਹੀਂ ਪੈਂਦੀ।
anand|anand24.line04.interpretiveCaution: The criticism concerns recitation separated from understanding and its spiritual grounding. It does not cancel the preceding invitation to sing the Guru’s Bani.

anand|anand24.line05.simpleEn: Maya has carried their attention away; their words remain an outward utterance.
anand|anand24.line05.simplePa: ਮਾਇਆ ਨੇ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਚਿੱਤ ਖਿੱਚ ਲਿਆ ਹੈ, ਉਹ ਉਪਰੋਂ ਉਪਰੋਂ ਹੀ ਬੋਲਦੇ ਰਹਿੰਦੇ ਹਨ।
anand|anand24.line05.interpretiveCaution: Hir laia expresses the mind being carried off. Ravani is read here as merely verbal or outward, following Sahib Singh’s contextual explanation; it is not praise for fluent speech.

anand|anand24.line06.simpleEn: Nanak says: without the True Guru, other speech remains spiritually unripe.
anand|anand24.line06.simplePa: ਨਾਨਕ ਆਖਦੇ ਹਨ: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਤੋਂ ਬਿਨਾ ਹੋਰ ਬਾਣੀ ਆਤਮਕ ਪੱਖੋਂ ਕੱਚੀ ਹੈ।
anand|anand24.line06.interpretiveCaution: The final line deliberately returns to the opening. Keep the Guru-centered claim rather than reducing the whole pauri to a general lesson about communication.

editorialAmendments.reason: Clarifies the relation of sahaj to finding the Guru; the earlier wording could make natural ease the manner or prerequisite of the encounter.

before.simpleEn: By meeting the True Guru with natural ease, a new celebration begins within my mind.
before.simplePa: ਸਹਜ ਨਾਲ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਿਲਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਮੇਰੇ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਦੀ ਵਧਾਈ ਗੂੰਜੀ।
before.interpretiveCaution: Sahaj means inward poise in this poetic context; it is not a clinically measured mood state or a prescribed meditation technique.

after.simpleEn: I have found the True Guru and inward steadiness; celebration resounds in my mind.
after.simplePa: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਮਿਲਣ ਨਾਲ ਮਨ ਸਹਜ ਵਿੱਚ ਟਿਕਿਆ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਦਰ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਧਾਈਆਂ ਗੂੰਜ ਰਹੀਆਂ ਹਨ।
after.interpretiveCaution: This working reading treats sahaj as inward poise accompanying the meeting with the Guru. It does not mean merely that meeting the Guru was easy, or prescribe a technique for producing a mood.

editorialAmendments.reason: Restores the continuing third-person subject and descriptive sense, which the earlier English wish and Punjabi first-person exhortation obscured.

before.simpleEn: May Your praise always be spoken, and may Your Naam abide in the mind.
before.simplePa: ਤੇਰੀ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ-ਸਲਾਹ ਸਦਾ ਕਰੀਏ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਮ ਨੂੰ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਸਾਈਏ।
before.interpretiveCaution: Praise and remembrance describe a way of living rather than an external prize or purchase.

after.simpleEn: That person continually praises You and keeps Your Naam within the mind.
after.simplePa: ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਤੇਰੀ ਦਾਤ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ, ਉਹ ਸਦਾ ਤੇਰੀ ਸਿਫ਼ਤ ਕਰਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਤੇਰਾ ਨਾਮ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਸਾਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
after.interpretiveCaution: The person receiving the gift in the preceding line remains the subject here. Praise and Naam describe that person’s life; the line is not a separate wish or a new first-person instruction.

editorialAmendments.reason: Clarifies the contextual musical sense of sabada ghanere instead of treating the plural as a definite set of canonical Shabads.

before.simpleEn: Those whose hearts hold Naam are pictured as filled with many resonant Shabads.
before.simplePa: ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾਮ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਅੰਦਰ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਗੂੰਜ ਦਿਖਾਈ ਗਈ ਹੈ।
before.interpretiveCaution: This sound imagery is poetic and not a claim that a particular audible frequency or track must play.

after.simpleEn: In minds where Naam dwells, many melodies of joy are pictured as resounding.
after.simplePa: ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਮਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾਮ ਵੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ, ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਅੰਦਰ ਮਾਨੋ ਅਨੰਦ ਦੀਆਂ ਅਨੇਕ ਸੁਰਾਂ ਗੂੰਜਦੀਆਂ ਹਨ।
after.interpretiveCaution: Sabada is read here in its musical sense of sounds or melodies. It should not automatically imply a collection of distinct canonical hymns, or require the reader to hear an actual sound.

editorialAmendments.reason: Explains the fivefold musical image without implying five identified canonical hymns. The recovered original Punjabi was valid UTF-8 and is retained in the audit fields; no encoding repair is claimed.

before.simpleEn: In the blessed inner home, five Shabads are pictured as sounding.
before.simplePa: ਭਾਗਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਹਿਰਦੇ-ਘਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੰਜ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਗੂੰਜ ਦੀ ਤਸਵੀਰ ਹੈ।
before.interpretiveCaution: “Five Shabads” and blessed home require qualified Sikh interpretive review; this is not evidence of five specific audio tracks or external sound waves.

after.simpleEn: In that fortunate inner home, a fivefold music of celebration is pictured as resounding.
after.simplePa: ਉਸ ਸੁਭਾਗੇ ਹਿਰਦੇ-ਘਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਾਨੋ ਪੰਜ ਕਿਸਮਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਜ਼ਾਂ ਦੀ ਸਾਂਝੀ ਧੁਨ ਵੱਜਦੀ ਹੈ।
after.interpretiveCaution: Panch sabad is read here as five kinds of musical sounds. This musical image is distinct from the five disruptive impulses in line three; neither five particular hymns nor five audible tones are prescribed.

editorialAmendments.reason: Restores the vocative address and the Guru as the giver of grace in this reading; the previous wording treated piaariaa as a title for the Divine.

before.simpleEn: True Anand is understood through the Guru and the grace of the Beloved One.
before.simplePa: ਸੱਚੇ ਅਨੰਦ ਦੀ ਸੂਝ ਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਤੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ।
before.interpretiveCaution: Anand here is a spiritual relationship, not a demand for constant pleasant mood or an emotional-performance score.

after.simpleEn: Dear one, Anand is always learned through the Guru, through the Guru’s grace.
after.simplePa: ਹੇ ਪਿਆਰੇ, ਅਨੰਦ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਸਦਾ ਗੁਰੂ ਤੋਂ ਹੀ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ, ਜਦ ਗੁਰੂ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
after.interpretiveCaution: In this grammatical reading, piaariaa addresses the dear listener and the Guru grants grace. Anand names spiritual understanding and relationship, not a demand for a constantly pleasant mood.

editorialAmendments.reason: Retains the existing supported Shabad-centred explanation while making a material alternative reading explicit, rather than presenting one interpretation as settled.

before.simpleEn: When attachment loosens from within, the true Shabad reshapes their understanding and living.
before.simplePa: ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਅੰਦਰਲਾ ਮੋਹ ਟੁੱਟਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੱਚਾ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਸੰਵਾਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
before.interpretiveCaution: Breaking moh refers to attachment, not rejecting family responsibilities or cutting off loving relationships.

after.simpleEn: When attachment loosens from within, the true Shabad reshapes their understanding and living.
after.simplePa: ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦਾ ਅੰਦਰਲਾ ਮੋਹ ਟੁੱਟਦਾ ਹੈ, ਸੱਚਾ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਸੰਵਾਰਦਾ ਹੈ।
after.interpretiveCaution: The main explanation retains the Shabad-centred reading. Prof. Sahib Singh instead reads sabadu as the person’s speech, made gracious by the True One as attachment falls away. These alternatives need qualified review; loosening moh does not mean abandoning loving relationships or family responsibilities.

editorialAmendments.reason: Replace an unsupported anatomical guess with the documented steadiness reading.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One described as beyond the limits of physical arms or ordinary force, a working sense needing review.
before.simplePa: ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਜੋ ਸਰੀਰਕ ਬਾਹਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਆਮ ਬਲ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਹੈ; ਅਰਥ ਦੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਬਾਕੀ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Abaha and Adhaha spellings are not adjudicated. The martial images praise the Divine; they do not instruct readers to be violent or promise invulnerability.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the steadfast One, whom nothing can displace.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਅਡੋਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਹਿਲਾਇਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
after.nuance: For Abahe, this working reading follows the movement-related root explained in the consulted commentary. The earlier reference to bodily arms was unsupported; the original spelling is unchanged.

editorialAmendments.reason: Use a consistent movement-related gloss for the repeated epithet.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One beyond the grasp of ordinary arms or force; the precise Abahe word sense remains under review.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਆਮ ਬਲ ਜਾਂ ਬਾਂਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਅਬਾਹੇ” ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਅਸਥਾਈ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: This cluster has multiple difficult lexical items. Do not claim certain literal translations for Abahe, Tribarge or Asarge until qualified textual review.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the One who remains unshaken.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਅਡੋਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਕਿਸੇ ਦੇ ਹਿਲਾਇਆਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਹਿਲਦਾ।
after.nuance: The same Abahe occurs in Chhand 6. This draft uses the same steadiness reading in both occurrences; it does not infer arms or bodily force from the spelling. Linguistic review remains open.

editorialAmendments.reason: Replace the unsupported fixed-form gloss and make the attested interpretive difference visible.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One not limited by a fixed form; the Ajūpe wording needs Sanskrit/Braj review.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਇੱਕ ਨਿਸ਼ਚਿਤ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੱਝਦਾ; “ਅਜੂਪੇ” ਦੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਲੋੜੀਂਦੀ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: This juxtaposes One and many; Abhute/Ajupe are working editorial glosses and must not be treated as a definitive doctrine about physical existence.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the unbound One, free from constraint.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਮੁਕਤ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਕਿਸੇ ਬੰਧਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਹੀਂ।
after.nuance: Ajupe is read here as freedom from bondage, supported by the consulted Narain Singh steek. The Bhai Vir Singh-derived commentary connects it with freedom from pain. These readings remain open for specialist comparison; neither makes Ajupe simply another word for formlessness.

editorialAmendments.reason: Restore the bodily-constituents sense documented in the Mahan Kosh entry.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One praised as beyond a created support or fixed dependence; “Nirdhate” requires a qualified gloss.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਬਣਾਏ ਆਸਰੇ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਨ੍ਰਿਧਾਤੇ” ਦੇ ਪੱਕੇ ਅਰਥ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਬਾਕੀ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Nirdhate and Nirghate are difficult Sanskrit/Braj epithets. These are working educational senses only, NOT verified morphological interpretations; no claim of immunity to harm.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the One not made from bodily elements.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਸਰੀਰ ਦੇ ਤੱਤਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਬਣਿਆ ਨਹੀਂ।
after.nuance: Nirdhate is related here to dhatu, the constituents of a body. This is a theological working gloss, not a scientific claim about matter. The earlier wording about dependence or support confused this epithet with a different idea.

editorialAmendments.reason: Remove the unsupported impurity gloss while retaining the attested movement sense.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One beyond being soiled or shaken; the exact old-form “Nirdhute” requires review.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਮੈਲ ਜਾਂ ਹਿਲਾਉ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਨ੍ਰਿਧੂਤੇ” ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਅਸਥਾਈ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Nirdhute/Abhute/Aloke are lexically complex and could admit more than one qualified reading. Assumption is documented, not asserted as standard scholarly translation.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the steady One, beyond being shaken.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਅਡੋਲ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਡੋਲਾਇਆ ਨਹੀਂ ਜਾ ਸਕਦਾ।
after.nuance: For Nirdhute, the consulted commentary connects the word with movement. The draft therefore uses steadiness and removes the earlier added stain or impurity gloss. This remains an educational reading pending linguistic review.

editorialAmendments.reason: Correct a mistaken negation and retain the temporal/worlds interpretive difference.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One transcending narrowly measured threefold categories; “Trimane” remains provisional.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਸੀਮਤ ਤਿੰਨ-ਭੇਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਤ੍ਰਿਮਾਨੇ” ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਅਸਥਾਈ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Nritape, Athape, Trimane and Nidhane require a specialist Braj/Sanskrit review; do not use the idea of a “treasury” as a promised financial reward.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the One revered in every age and realm.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਹਰ ਕਾਲ ਅਤੇ ਹਰ ਲੋਕ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੰਨਣਯੋਗ ਹੈ।
after.nuance: Trimane is an affirmative title of reverence. Consulted readings connect its threefold reference with past, present and future, or with the three worlds. This broad paraphrase leaves that distinction open; it does not invent a negative prefix meaning beyond categories.

editorialAmendments.reason: Replace an unexplained generic threefold negation with an attributed working interpretation.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One beyond limiting threefold categories or pursuits; the exact Tribarge use needs scholarly checking.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਸੀਮਤ ਤਿੰਨ-ਭੇਦਾਂ ਜਾਂ ਲਾਲਸਾਵਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਤ੍ਰਿਬਰਗੇ” ਦੀ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: This cluster has multiple difficult lexical items. Do not claim certain literal translations for Abahe, Tribarge or Asarge until qualified textual review.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the One expressed through the three qualities of nature.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਕੁਦਰਤ ਦੇ ਤਿੰਨਾਂ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਵੀ ਪ੍ਰਗਟ ਹੁੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
after.nuance: This working reading of Tribarge follows the consulted Bhai Vir Singh-derived account of the three gunas: sattva, rajas and tamas. Other teaching traditions gloss the epithet differently. The exact compound remains under review; this line is not a settled definition of Divine nature.

editorialAmendments.reason: Resolve the English/Punjabi mismatch using a documented bliss-related reading.

before.simpleEn: I bow to the One related to every experience and enjoyment, yet not bounded by it; Prabhoge is a working sense.
before.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜੋ ਜੀਵਾਂ ਦੇ ਭੋਗ ਤੇ ਅਨੁਭਵ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਹੈ; “ਪ੍ਰਭੋਗੇ” ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਅਸਥਾਈ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Prabhoge/Sujoge require qualified interpretation, and the critique of colour is about Divine transcendence, never caste, race or human worth.

after.simpleEn: I bow to the One whose joy is complete.
after.simplePa: ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ ਜਿਸ ਦਾ ਆਨੰਦ ਪੂਰਨ ਹੈ।
after.nuance: Prabhoge is read here through supreme enjoyment or bliss. Both language drafts now express that same working reading. This does not settle every sense of bhog or promise that a reader will always feel happy.

editorialAmendments.reason: Remove the assumption that Ajupe is a fixed-form epithet; keep the source-specific interpretive comparison.

before.simpleEn: One Divine reality is invoked through both unity and many expressions, while remaining beyond fixed created form.
before.simplePa: ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਇਕਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਪ੍ਰਗਟਾਵਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਉਹ ਬਣੇ ਰੂਪਾਂ ਤਕ ਸੀਮਤ ਨਹੀਂ।

study.focus: One and many held together in praise.
study.closeReading: The first line greets the One, the second invokes the Many, and the remaining two use complex epithets relating to created and defined forms. The meaningful interpretive move is not to treat these as contradictions, but to explore the difference between the one unbounded Source and its diverse expressions. The exact old-word morphology has not been independently settled.
study.care: Abhute and Ajupe remain provisional working glosses. Do not present a precise cosmological mechanism or equate religious metaphor with scientific measurements.
study.reflection: Where might I see unity without denying genuine differences?
study.teachBack: Which first two words set up this chhand’s central comparison?

after.simpleEn: The One is praised through unity and multiplicity, with further titles whose precise meanings need careful comparison.
after.simplePa: ਇੱਕ ਅਤੇ ਅਨੇਕ ਦੇ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ; ਅਗਲੇ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਣਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਸਮਝਣ ਤੇ ਪਰਖਣ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Unity, multiplicity and the limits of a short gloss.
study.closeReading: The first pair places One beside Many. The next pair must be read on its own terms rather than treated as two interchangeable words for form. Abhute concerns created or elemental existence in the working draft; Ajupe is rendered here through freedom from constraint, with another documented reading noted beside the line. Comparing these meanings is part of the lesson, not a reason to alter the source.
study.care: The Ajupe line retains an explicit alternative reading. These explanatory choices are provisional and should not be turned into a definitive account of cosmology or an official lexical judgment.
study.reflection: Can I notice both a shared ground and real differences without flattening either?
study.teachBack: Which two opening titles form a contrast, and why should the last two be examined separately?

editorialAmendments.reason: Align the Study explanation with the corrected dhatu-related line meaning.

before.simpleEn: Names, desire and the causes of loss do not confine the One in this poetic salutation.
before.simplePa: ਨਾਂ, ਚਾਹ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਸ-ਵਿਨਾਸ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਉਪਰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A source-specific study of four difficult epithets.
study.closeReading: The opening lines invoke the One beyond a fixed name and without grasping desire. The second pair uses the harder Nirdhate/Nirghate forms, which have not been philologically adjudicated. These later terms should be taught as tentative meanings with explicit uncertainty, rather than building large doctrinal conclusions on an unverified short gloss.
study.care: Nirdhate and Nirghate are not approved dictionary definitions. Do not promise bodily invulnerability or suggest the Divine commands harmful behaviour.
study.reflection: How do names help us learn while still limiting what they describe?
study.teachBack: Which two familiar words precede the more difficult pair requiring specialist review?

after.simpleEn: The salutations move through name, desire, bodily constituents and destruction as limits that do not define the One.
after.simplePa: ਨਾਮ, ਚਾਹ, ਸਰੀਰ ਦੇ ਤੱਤ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਸ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਨਾ ਬੱਝਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Distinguishing a body’s constituents from its support.
study.closeReading: The first two titles concern naming and desire. The third is now explained through bodily constituents rather than dependence on an external support. The fourth concerns destruction or harm. Reading the four separately helps prevent a plausible general idea about God from being substituted for the particular word on the page. Each salutation still addresses the same One.
words: Not defined by a name; working gloss
study.care: Nirdhate receives a documented constituent-related reading, while exact historical morphology still needs specialist review. Praise of the Divine does not imply that a person can become physically immune to harm.
study.reflection: When can a familiar idea keep me from noticing what a text actually says?
study.teachBack: How is a description about bodily constituents different from a description about needing support?

editorialAmendments.reason: Remove the unsupported stain interpretation from the summary, close reading and vocabulary.

before.simpleEn: The chhand addresses the One beyond ordinary stain, worldly form, limited perception and sorrow.
before.simplePa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਮੈਲ, ਬਣੇ ਰੂਪ, ਆਮ ਨਿਗਾਹ ਅਤੇ ਸੋਗ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The limits of appearance and the language of sorrow.
study.closeReading: These four names form a cluster of negations. The specific meanings of Nirdhute, Abhute and Aloke are provisional, while Asoke invites a relatively clear contrast with sorrow. The reader can learn how Braj salutation syntax works without pretending every compound has one certain English equivalent.
study.care: Do not equate “without sorrow” with a clinical guarantee or suggest that anyone experiencing grief has failed spiritually. Linguistic review is open.
study.reflection: What is the difference between respecting grief and finding hope in a spiritual text?
study.teachBack: Which of these four titles most directly names sorrow?

after.simpleEn: This sequence praises steadiness and freedom from created limitations, ordinary sight and sorrow.
after.simplePa: ਇਹ ਲੜੀ ਅਡੋਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸਿਰਜੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ, ਆਮ ਨਿਗਾਹ ਤੇ ਸੋਗ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Giving each repeated salutation its own meaning.
study.closeReading: Four salutations share a repeated opening but differ in their descriptive words. The first is read through steadiness, without adding an unsupported claim about stain. Abhute and Aloke then introduce different interpretive questions about created existence and seeing. Asoke brings sorrow into the sequence. The repetition is a reason to listen carefully for the changing title, rather than to assume all four mean the same thing.
words: Steady or not shaken; working gloss
study.care: The revised first gloss follows a movement-related reading; the remaining old-language details are still provisional. Describing the Divine as free from sorrow is not a demand that human beings suppress grief.
study.reflection: What changes when I attend to a repeated phrase instead of rushing past it?
study.teachBack: How does the fourth title differ in subject from the first title?

editorialAmendments.reason: Correct the falsely negative account of Trimane in the deeper explanation.

before.simpleEn: The poem bows to a One beyond ordinary affliction or establishment and describes inexhaustible treasure.
before.simplePa: ਕਵੀ ਆਮ ਤਾਪ ਤੇ ਠਿਕਾਣੇ ਦੀ ਹੱਦ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਕਰਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਨਿਧਾਨ ਆਖਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Unsettled old vocabulary beside the image of a treasury.
study.closeReading: The sequence moves through Nritape and Athape, followed by Trimane and Nidhane. Nidhane suggests a repository or treasury, while the preceding forms need close textual and morphological attention. Rather than asserting a sure “three worlds” or “three gunas” gloss, the Study layer should leave the third term openly unresolved until a qualified scholar can compare dictionaries and textual witnesses.
words: Treasury, source or store of gifts
study.care: “Treasure” is devotional praise and not evidence of financial returns; Trimane’s meaning is unsettled and should not be inserted as a certain doctrine.
study.reflection: How can I learn to hold an unresolved word without making up certainty?
study.teachBack: Which term in the fourth line introduces the treasury image?

after.simpleEn: The sequence moves from freedom from affliction and dependence on establishment to reverence and the image of treasure.
after.simplePa: ਛੰਦ ਤਾਪ ਅਤੇ ਕਿਸੇ ਦੇ ਸਥਾਪਿਤ ਕੀਤੇ ਹੋਣ ਤੋਂ ਰਹਿਤ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ, ਫਿਰ ਉਸ ਦੇ ਮਾਣ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਧਾਨ-ਰੂਪ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: An affirmative title within a sequence of negations.
study.closeReading: The first two descriptive titles have negative force, but that pattern must not automatically be extended to the third. Trimane affirms reverence; its precise threefold reference has more than one documented explanation. Nidhane then introduces a treasury image. The sequence therefore changes its rhetorical movement, and that change would be lost by translating every unfamiliar title as beyond something.
words: Revered across the three times or worlds; working alternatives
study.care: The temporal and worlds-based readings of Trimane need qualified comparison. The title is not being treated as a claim about measured dimensions, and the treasury image does not promise material reward.
study.reflection: Do I let an apparent pattern decide a word’s meaning before I examine it?
study.teachBack: Why should the negative sense of the first two titles not be imposed on Trimane?

editorialAmendments.reason: Remove the arms gloss and the unsupported blanket description beyond categories.

before.simpleEn: The One is praised as unfathomable and beyond ordinary reach, categories and created origin.
before.simplePa: ਅਥਾਹ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਆਮ ਪਹੁੰਚ, ਵੰਡ ਅਤੇ ਸ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਟੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਨਮਸਕਾਰ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A cluster of attributes requiring source comparison.
study.closeReading: Agahe points toward unfathomability, while Abahe, Tribarge and Asarge carry additional old-language possibilities. This chhand is useful for learning to distinguish an easy general religious idea from a precise word-level translation. The final three terms should remain visibly provisional until review, even though the four original source lines themselves are fully displayed.
study.care: Uncertain Braj/Sanskrit words require qualified review, not a silent source correction. No word here is authority for a physical or medical experiment.
study.reflection: What is gained by acknowledging the limits of an explanation?
study.teachBack: Which title begins the chhand and what general theme does it establish?

after.simpleEn: The One is praised as unfathomable, steadfast and uncreated; the threefold title carries a provisional reading.
after.simplePa: ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਅਥਾਹਤਾ, ਅਡੋਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਅਜਨਮੇ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਵਡਿਆਈ ਹੈ; ਤਿੰਨਾਂ ਗੁਣਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ਣ ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਹਾਲੇ ਸਮੀਖਿਆ ਅਧੀਨ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A repeated title and a distinct threefold expression.
study.closeReading: Agahe opens the chhand with the difficulty of fathoming the One. Abahe repeats a title from Chhand 6 and is explained consistently through steadiness. Tribarge introduces a different threefold expression; the line note identifies the working interpretation used here instead of disguising it as a settled lexical result. Asarge closes the sequence by addressing the One as uncreated. These four titles need not all be paraphrased with the same negative formula.
study.care: The threefold reference in Tribarge remains a matter for specialist comparison. A theological description of the gunas is not a scientific classification of people or a measure of their worth.
study.reflection: What makes a clear statement of uncertainty more useful than a vague explanation?
study.teachBack: Which title also occurs in Chhand 6, and which title has the explicitly provisional threefold reading?

editorialAmendments.reason: Align the Study discussion with the corrected bilingual opening line.

before.simpleEn: The chhand praises a sustaining One beyond limiting colour and disintegration.
before.simplePa: ਇਹ ਛੰਦ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵਨ ਦਾ ਮੂਲ, ਰੰਗ-ਹੱਦਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਪਰੇ ਅਤੇ ਅਭੰਗ ਦੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: Enjoyment, relationship and transcendence in four titles.
study.closeReading: Prabhoge and Sujoge are difficult source words for which the draft offers only a provisional sense. The final pair is more clearly structured around absence of limiting colour and indestructibility. The student is invited to notice how devotional naming moves from relation with the world to a reality that cannot be assigned one human appearance or broken apart.
study.care: Never use the absence of colour to rank human skin tones, caste or race. No explanation here proves invulnerability to harm; Prabhoge/Sujoge need human review.
study.reflection: How might I look beyond appearance when assessing someone’s character?
study.teachBack: How do the last two descriptive titles differ from the first two?

after.simpleEn: The opening invokes complete Divine joy and fitting union; the final pair turns to colour and indestructibility.
after.simplePa: ਸ਼ੁਰੂ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੂਰਨ ਰੱਬੀ ਆਨੰਦ ਅਤੇ ਸੁਚੱਜੇ ਮਿਲਾਪ ਨੂੰ ਯਾਦ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ; ਅਖੀਰਲੀ ਜੋੜੀ ਰੰਗ ਅਤੇ ਅਭੰਗਤਾ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਦੀ ਹੈ।

study.focus: A shared meaning across the two teaching languages.
study.closeReading: The revised opening explanation presents the same bliss-related working sense in English and Punjabi. Sujoge then introduces the question of fitting union or relationship, whose precise interpretation remains provisional. The final two titles change direction toward colour and what cannot be broken. The student can notice that movement without assuming that a short translation exhausts any of these words.
words: Not broken or destroyed; working gloss
study.care: Prabhoge and Sujoge remain interpretive working readings. The description of Divine joy does not require a constant human mood, and language about colour must not be used to rank skin tones or caste.
study.reflection: How can two explanations in different languages support the same careful understanding?
study.teachBack: How does the final pair of titles change the focus introduced by the opening pair?

editorialAmendments.reason: Remove the unsupported lotus narrative and restore the source’s connected images of burning water, attachment as mud and a foot unable to move.

before.simpleEn: The mind is likened to a lotus entangled in a muddy pond of attachment; the refrain asks why the foolish mind forgets the One, and the speaker humbly seeks those who keep the Divine in remembrance.
before.simplePa: ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਮੋਹ ਦੇ ਚਿੱਕੜ ਵਿੱਚ ਫਸੇ ਕੰਵਲ ਵਾਂਗ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਹੈ; ਰਹਾਉ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਯਾਦ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਅਤੇ ਕਵੀ ਨਾਮ ਨਾ ਭੁੱਲਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ ਮੰਗਦਾ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: Mud, drowning and an unwise mind are spiritual metaphors. They do not describe psychiatric illness, disability, caste or a literal physical drowning event. The source record contains a full hymn.
before.sourceContext: REHRAS_ORIGINAL_AGGREGATED_TUK_RECORD; sggs family; summary not literal per-tuk translation

after.simpleEn: The hymn pictures life in a pool whose water burns with craving, with feet caught in the mud of attachment; the refrain calls the forgetful mind back to the One, and the speaker seeks those who keep the Divine in remembrance.
after.simplePa: ਜੀਵਨ ਨੂੰ ਅਜਿਹੇ ਸਰੋਵਰ ਨਾਲ ਜੋੜਿਆ ਹੈ ਜਿੱਥੇ ਤ੍ਰਿਸ਼ਨਾ ਦੀ ਅੱਗ ਅਤੇ ਮੋਹ ਦਾ ਚਿੱਕੜ ਪੈਰ ਰੋਕਦੇ ਹਨ; ਰਹਾਉ ਮਨ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਵੱਲ ਮੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਨੂੰ ਨਾ ਭੁੱਲਣ ਵਾਲਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ ਮੰਗੀ ਹੈ।
after.nuance: The consulted readings understand pank ju moh as the mud of attachment in this sentence, not a lotus. The frozen source spelling is unchanged. Fire, mud and drowning describe spiritual entanglement; this full-hymn summary is not a diagnosis or a literal account of a physical event.
after.sourceContext: REHRAS_ORIGINAL_AGGREGATED_TUK_RECORD; sggs family; summary not literal per-tuk translation

editorialAmendments.reason: Align both languages with the final tuk’s attribution of speech to Divine grace; the original Punjabi incorrectly summarized that ending as a request for grace.

before.simpleEn: The poet takes refuge at the Divine feet, declining to make another ultimate refuge; Rama, Rahim and named scriptural traditions appear in a strong comparison that ends with the poet relying on Asipan’s grace.
before.simplePa: ਕਵੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਚਰਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਹੋਰ ਅੰਤਿਮ ਆਸਰਾ ਨਾ ਭਾਲਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ; ਰਾਮ-ਰਹੀਮ ਤੇ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥਾਂ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਕਰਕੇ ਅੰਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਸਿਪਾਨ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਮੰਗਦਾ ਹੈ।
before.nuance: This is the EVENING Pae Gahe Savaiya, not the ten morning Sravag Sudh verses. The critique of religious paths must never be used to demean believers of other traditions. The original record includes multiple poetic tuks.
before.sourceContext: REHRAS_ORIGINAL_AGGREGATED_TUK_RECORD; dasam family; summary not literal per-tuk translation

after.simpleEn: The poet takes refuge at the Divine feet, declining to make another ultimate refuge; Rama, Rahim and named scriptural traditions appear in a strong comparison that ends by attributing the words spoken to Asipan’s grace.
after.simplePa: ਕਵੀ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੇ ਚਰਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਸ਼ਰਨ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਹੋਰ ਅੰਤਿਮ ਆਸਰਾ ਨਾ ਭਾਲਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ; ਰਾਮ-ਰਹੀਮ ਤੇ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਗ੍ਰੰਥਾਂ ਦਾ ਜ਼ਿਕਰ ਕਰਕੇ ਅੰਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਆਪਣੇ ਕਹੇ ਬਚਨਾਂ ਦਾ ਸਿਹਰਾ ਅਸਿਪਾਨ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨੂੰ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।
after.nuance: This is the evening Pae Gahe Savaiya, distinct from the ten morning Sravag Sudh verses. Its closing credits Divine grace for the utterance, rather than merely asking for future grace. The strong comparison of traditions does not authorize contempt for their believers; this is a summary of multiple tuks.
after.sourceContext: REHRAS_ORIGINAL_AGGREGATED_TUK_RECORD; dasam family; summary not literal per-tuk translation

editorialAmendments.reason: Remove the lotus error from focus, close reading, vocabulary and teach-back while retaining the original supported bilingual summary and reflection.

before.simpleEn: The mind caught in the muddy pool of attachment is invited to turn again toward the One through remembrance and humility.
before.simplePa: ਮੋਹ ਦੇ ਚਿੱਕੜ ਵਿੱਚ ਫਸਿਆ ਮਨ ਨਾਮ ਦੀ ਯਾਦ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਰਾਹੀਂ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਵੱਲ ਮੁੜਨ ਦੀ ਸੇਧ ਪਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।

study.focus: The image of the lotus in a pond of attachment.
study.closeReading: The original source record contains a whole short hymn, starting with dwelling in a muddy pond and the lotus whose foot cannot move. The refrain addresses the unwise mind for forgetting the One. The poet does not boast of personal religious purity, but describes a vulnerable life and seeks refuge with those who do not forget the Divine.
